206	    pub fn with_overrides(home: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
207	        let mut registry = Self::builtin()?;
208	        let overrides_dir = home.join("providers.d");
209	        let mut paths = match fs::read_dir(&overrides_dir) {
210	            Ok(entries) => entries
211	                .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
212	                .map(|entry| entry.path())
213	                .filter(|path| path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("toml"))
214	                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
215	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(registry),
216	            Err(source) => {
217	                return Err(ProviderError::Io {
218	                    path: overrides_dir.display().to_string(),
219	                    source,
220	                });
221	            }
222	        };
223	        paths.sort();
224	        for path in paths {
225	            registry.load_override(&path)?;
226	        }
227	        Ok(registry)
228	    }

250	    fn load_override(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
251	        let raw = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
252	            path: path.display().to_string(),
253	            source,
254	        })?;
255	        let mut override_value = parse_toml_value(&raw, path)?;
256	        let id = descriptor_id_from_value(&override_value)
257	            .or_else(|| id_from_path(path))
258	            .ok_or_else(|| {
259	                ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
260	                    "provider override {} must include id",
261	                    path.display()
262	                ))
263	            })?;
264	        ensure_id(&mut override_value, &id)?;
265	        let merged = if let Some(existing) = self.descriptors.get(&id) {
266	            let mut base = descriptor_to_value(existing)?;
267	            merge_values(&mut base, override_value);
268	            base
269	        } else {
270	            override_value
271	        };
272	        let descriptor = value_to_descriptor(merged, path)?;
273	        self.descriptors.insert(descriptor.id.clone(), descriptor);
274	        Ok(())
275	    }
276	}

342	        );
343	    };
344	    if let Some(probe) = descriptor.version_probe.as_ref()
345	        && !probe.args.is_empty()
346	    {
347	        match Command::new(&location).args(&probe.args).output() {
348	            Ok(output) => {
349	                if !output.status.success() {
350	                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
351	                    return base_probe_result(
352	                        descriptor,
353	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
354	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
355	                        None,
356	                        "missing",
357	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
358	                        Some(trim_probe_message(&stderr)),
359	                    );
360	                }
361	                let version = trim_probe_message(&format!(
362	                    "{}{}",
363	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
364	                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
365	                ));
366	                if let Some(expected) = probe.expect_substring.as_deref()
367	                    && !version.contains(expected)
368	                {
369	                    return base_probe_result(
370	                        descriptor,
371	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
372	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
373	                        Some(version),
374	                        "missing",
375	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
376	                        Some(format!("version output did not contain {expected}")),
377	                    );
378	                }
379	                if let Some(min) = probe.min_known_good.as_deref()
380	                    && !version_at_least(&version, min)
381	                {
382	                    return base_probe_result(
383	                        descriptor,
384	                        ProbeStatus::Failed,
385	                        Some(location.display().to_string()),
386	                        Some(version),
387	                        "missing",
388	                        Some(ProbeErrorKind::VersionMismatch),
389	                        Some(format!("version below known-good {min}")),
390	                    );
391	                }
392	                return base_probe_result(
393	                    descriptor,
394	                    ProbeStatus::Ok,
395	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
396	                    Some(version),
397	                    "ready",
398	                    None,
399	                    None,
400	                );
401	            }
402	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
403	                return base_probe_result(
404	                    descriptor,
405	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
406	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
407	                    None,
408	                    "missing",
409	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::PermissionDenied),
410	                    Some(format!("permission denied running {binary}")),
411	                );
412	            }
413	            Err(source) => {
414	                return base_probe_result(
415	                    descriptor,
416	                    ProbeStatus::Failed,
417	                    Some(location.display().to_string()),
418	                    None,
419	                    "missing",
420	                    Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
421	                    Some(source.to_string()),
422	                );
423	            }
424	        }
425	    }
426	    base_probe_result(
427	        descriptor,
428	        ProbeStatus::Ok,
429	        Some(location.display().to_string()),
430	        None,
431	        "ready",
432	        None,
433	        None,
434	    )
435	}

437	async fn probe_http_descriptor(
438	    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
439	    options: ProviderProbeOptions,
440	) -> ProviderProbeResult {
441	    if let AuthKind::ApiKey = descriptor.auth.kind {
442	        let Some(env_var) = descriptor.auth.env_var.as_deref() else {
443	            return base_probe_result(
444	                descriptor,
445	                ProbeStatus::Failed,
446	                descriptor.default_endpoint.clone(),
447	                None,
448	                "missing",
449	                Some(ProbeErrorKind::AuthMissing),
450	                Some("api-key provider has no env var configured".to_string()),
451	            );
452	        };
453	        if std::env::var(env_var)
454	            .ok()
455	            .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
456	            .is_none()
457	        {
458	            return base_probe_result(
459	                descriptor,
460	                ProbeStatus::Failed,
461	                descriptor.default_endpoint.clone(),
462	                None,
463	                "missing",
464	                Some(ProbeErrorKind::AuthMissing),
465	                Some(format!("{env_var} missing")),
466	            );
467	        }
468	    }
469	    if options.ping {
470	        return ping_endpoint(descriptor).await;
471	    }
472	    base_probe_result(
473	        descriptor,
474	        ProbeStatus::Ok,
475	        descriptor.default_endpoint.clone(),
476	        Some("ping skipped".to_string()),
477	        "ready",
478	        None,
479	        None,
480	    )
481	}
482	
483	async fn probe_local_http_descriptor(
484	    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
485	    options: ProviderProbeOptions,
486	) -> ProviderProbeResult {
487	    if options.ping {
488	        return ping_endpoint(descriptor).await;
489	    }
490	    base_probe_result(
491	        descriptor,
492	        ProbeStatus::Skipped,
493	        descriptor.default_endpoint.clone(),
494	        Some("ping required".to_string()),
495	        "unknown",
496	        None,
497	        Some("local endpoint probe skipped; pass --ping".to_string()),
498	    )

500	
501	async fn ping_endpoint(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderProbeResult {
502	    let endpoint = descriptor.default_endpoint.clone().unwrap_or_default();
503	    let client = match reqwest::Client::builder()
504	        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
505	        .build()
506	    {
507	        Ok(client) => client,
508	        Err(source) => {
509	            return base_probe_result(
510	                descriptor,
511	                ProbeStatus::Failed,
512	                Some(endpoint),
513	                None,
514	                "missing",
515	                Some(ProbeErrorKind::ProbeFailed),
516	                Some(source.to_string()),
517	            );
518	        }
519	    };
520	    match client.get(&endpoint).send().await {
521	        Ok(response) => base_probe_result(
522	            descriptor,
523	            ProbeStatus::Ok,
524	            Some(endpoint),
525	            Some(format!("HTTP {}", response.status())),
526	            "ready",
527	            None,
528	            None,
529	        ),
530	        Err(source) => base_probe_result(
531	            descriptor,
532	            ProbeStatus::Failed,
533	            Some(endpoint),
534	            None,
535	            "missing",
536	            Some(ProbeErrorKind::EndpointUnreachable),
537	            Some(source.to_string()),
538	        ),
539	    }
540	}

542	fn base_probe_result(
543	    descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor,
544	    status: ProbeStatus,
545	    location: Option<String>,
546	    version: Option<String>,
547	    credential: &str,
548	    error_kind: Option<ProbeErrorKind>,
549	    message: Option<String>,
550	) -> ProviderProbeResult {
551	    ProviderProbeResult {
552	        id: descriptor.id.clone(),
553	        display_name: descriptor.display_name.clone(),
554	        kind: descriptor.kind.clone(),
555	        status,
556	        location,
557	        version,
558	        credential: credential.to_string(),
559	        subscription: descriptor.subscription,
560	        metering: if descriptor.subscription {
561	            "subscription".to_string()
562	        } else {
563	            "metered".to_string()
564	        },
565	        fs_artifacts: descriptor
566	            .fs_detection_paths
567	            .iter()
568	            .map(|path| expand_home_path(path).display().to_string())
569	            .collect(),
570	        error_kind,
571	        message,
572	        try_lines: descriptor.install_hint.try_lines.clone(),
573	    }
574	}
575	
576	fn resolve_binary(binary: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
577	    let configured = PathBuf::from(binary);
578	    if configured.components().count() > 1 || configured.is_absolute() {
579	        return configured.exists().then_some(configured);
580	    }
581	    which::which(binary).ok()
582	}
583	
584	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
585	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
586	        return path.to_path_buf();
587	    };
588	    if path == Path::new("~") {
589	        return home;
590	    }
591	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
592	        return home.join(rest);
593	    }
594	    path.to_path_buf()
595	}
596	
597	fn trim_probe_message(message: &str) -> String {
598	    let first_line = message
599	        .lines()
600	        .find(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
601	        .unwrap_or("");
602	    let trimmed = first_line.trim();
603	    if trimmed.len() > 120 {
604	        format!("{}...", &trimmed[..120])
605	    } else {
606	        trimmed.to_string()
607	    }
608	}
609	
610	fn version_at_least(output: &str, minimum: &str) -> bool {
611	    let observed = first_version_tuple(output);
612	    let required = first_version_tuple(minimum);
613	    if observed.is_empty() || required.is_empty() {
614	        return output >= minimum;
615	    }
616	    compare_version_tuples(&observed, &required) != std::cmp::Ordering::Less
617	}
618	
619	fn first_version_tuple(text: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
620	    text.split(|ch: char| !ch.is_ascii_digit() && ch != '.')
621	        .find(|part| part.chars().any(|ch| ch.is_ascii_digit()))
622	        .unwrap_or("")
623	        .split('.')
624	        .filter_map(|part| part.parse::<u64>().ok())
625	        .collect()
626	}
627	
628	fn compare_version_tuples(left: &[u64], right: &[u64]) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
629	    let len = left.len().max(right.len());
630	    for index in 0..len {
631	        let l = left.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
632	        let r = right.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0);
633	        match l.cmp(&r) {
634	            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
635	            ordering => return ordering,
636	        }
637	    }
638	    std::cmp::Ordering::Equal
639	}
640	
641	fn split_command_line(command: &str) -> Vec<String> {
642	    let mut args = Vec::new();
643	    let mut current = String::new();
644	    let mut quote = None::<char>;
645	    let mut escaped = false;
646	    for ch in command.chars() {
647	        if escaped {
648	            current.push(ch);
649	            escaped = false;
650	            continue;
651	        }
652	        if ch == '\\' {
653	            escaped = true;
654	            continue;
655	        }
656	        if let Some(active_quote) = quote {
657	            if ch == active_quote {
658	                quote = None;
659	            } else {
660	                current.push(ch);
661	            }
662	            continue;
663	        }
664	        match ch {
665	            '"' | '\'' => quote = Some(ch),
666	            ' ' | '\t' | '\n' => {
667	                if !current.is_empty() {
668	                    args.push(current.clone());
669	                    current.clear();
670	                }
671	            }
672	            _ => current.push(ch),
673	        }
674	    }
675	    if !current.is_empty() {
676	        args.push(current);
677	    }
678	    args
679	}

724	
725	fn merge_values(base: &mut Value, override_value: Value) {
726	    match (base, override_value) {
727	        (Value::Table(base_table), Value::Table(override_table)) => {
728	            for (key, value) in override_table {
729	                match base_table.get_mut(&key) {
730	                    Some(base_value) => merge_values(base_value, value),
731	                    None => {
732	                        base_table.insert(key, value);
733	                    }
734	                }
735	            }
736	        }
737	        (base_value, override_value) => *base_value = override_value,
738	    }
739	}

26	// isDirOrSymlink reports whether the entry is a directory or a
27	// symlink that resolves to a directory. parentDir is needed to
28	// build the full path for symlink resolution.
29	func isDirOrSymlink(
30		entry os.DirEntry, parentDir string,
31	) bool {
32		if entry.IsDir() {
33			return true
34		}
35		if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
36			return false
37		}
38		fi, err := os.Stat(

40		)
41		if err != nil || fi == nil {
42			return false
43		}
44		return fi.IsDir()
45	}

57

60		OpenCodeSourceStorage OpenCodeSourceMode = "storage"
61		OpenCodeSourceSQLite  OpenCodeSourceMode = "sqlite"

64	// OpenCodeSource describes the resolved storage backend for an

66	type OpenCodeSource struct {
67		Mode        OpenCodeSourceMode
68		Root        string
69		SessionRoot string
70		DBPath      string
71	}
72	
73	// ResolveOpenCodeSource detects whether an OpenCode root is using
74	// file-backed storage or legacy SQLite storage.
75	func ResolveOpenCodeSource(root string) OpenCodeSource {
76		if root == "" {
77			return OpenCodeSource{}
78		}
79	
80		sessionRoot := filepath.Join(root, "storage", "session")
81		if info, err := os.Stat(sessionRoot); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
82			return OpenCodeSource{
83				Mode:        OpenCodeSourceStorage,
84				Root:        root,
85				SessionRoot: sessionRoot,
86				DBPath:      filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db"),
87			}
88		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
89			storageRoot := filepath.Join(root, "storage")
90			if info, serr := os.Stat(storageRoot); serr == nil && info.IsDir() {
91				return OpenCodeSource{
92					Mode:        OpenCodeSourceStorage,
93					Root:        root,
94					SessionRoot: sessionRoot,
95					DBPath:      filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db"),
96				}
97			}
98		}
99	
100		dbPath := filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db")
101		if info, err := os.Stat(dbPath); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
102			return OpenCodeSource{
103				Mode:   OpenCodeSourceSQLite,
104				Root:   root,
105				DBPath: dbPath,
106			}
107		}
108	
109		return OpenCodeSource{Root: root}
110	}
111	
112	// DiscoverOpenCodeSessions finds all file-backed OpenCode session
113	// JSON files under storage/session.
114	func DiscoverOpenCodeSessions(root string) []DiscoveredFile {
115		src := ResolveOpenCodeSource(root)
116		if src.Mode != OpenCodeSourceStorage {
117			return nil
118		}
119	
120		var files []DiscoveredFile
121		entries, err := os.ReadDir(src.SessionRoot)
122		if err != nil {
123			return nil
124		}
125		for _, entry := range entries {
126			if !isDirOrSymlink(entry, src.SessionRoot) {
127				continue
128			}
129			projectDir := filepath.Join(src.SessionRoot, entry.Name())
130			sessionEntries, err := os.ReadDir(projectDir)
131			if err != nil {
132				continue
133			}
134			for _, sessionEntry := range sessionEntries {
135				if sessionEntry.IsDir() ||
136					!strings.HasSuffix(sessionEntry.Name(), ".json") {
137					continue
138				}
139				path := filepath.Join(projectDir, sessionEntry.Name())
140				files = append(files, DiscoveredFile{
141					Path:    path,
142					Project: openCodeSessionProject(path),
143					Agent:   AgentOpenCode,
144				})
145			}
146		}
147	
148		sort.Slice(files, func(i, j int) bool {
149			return files[i].Path < files[j].Path
150		})
151		return files
152	}
153	
154	// FindOpenCodeSourceFile locates a single OpenCode session source
155	// path or SQLite backing file by raw session ID. Returns "" when
156	// the session is not present under this root so the caller
157	// (Engine.FindSourceFile) can continue searching later configured
158	// roots — important when an early hybrid root with an unrelated
159	// opencode.db could otherwise shadow a session in a later root.
160	func FindOpenCodeSourceFile(root, sessionID string) string {
161		if !IsValidSessionID(sessionID) {
162			return ""
163		}
164	
165		src := ResolveOpenCodeSource(root)
166		switch src.Mode {
167		case OpenCodeSourceStorage:
168			if entries, err := os.ReadDir(src.SessionRoot); err == nil {
169				for _, entry := range entries {
170					if !isDirOrSymlink(entry, src.SessionRoot) {
171						continue
172					}
173					path := filepath.Join(
174						src.SessionRoot, entry.Name(),
175						sessionID+".json",
176					)
177					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil &&
178						!info.IsDir() {
179						return path
180					}
181				}
182			}
183			if OpenCodeSQLiteSessionExists(src.DBPath, sessionID) {
184				return OpenCodeSQLiteVirtualPath(
185					src.DBPath, sessionID,
186				)
187			}
188			return ""
189		case OpenCodeSourceSQLite:
190			if OpenCodeSQLiteSessionExists(src.DBPath, sessionID) {
191				return OpenCodeSQLiteVirtualPath(
192					src.DBPath, sessionID,
193				)
194			}
195			return ""
196		default:
197			return ""
198		}
199	}

376	// StripHostPrefix splits a remote session ID into its host
377	// and raw ID parts. Remote IDs use the form "host~rawID"
378	// where the "~" separator avoids conflict with both agent
379	// prefixes (":") and URL path segments ("/"). For local
380	// session IDs (no "~" present), host is empty and rawID is
381	// the original ID.
382	func StripHostPrefix(id string) (host, rawID string) {
383		if before, after, ok := strings.Cut(id, "~"); ok {
384			return before, after
385		}
386		return "", id
387	}

135	fn resolve_cli_binary(binary: &str) -> ResolvedCliBinary {
136	    let configured = PathBuf::from(binary);
137	    let located = if configured.components().count() > 1 || configured.is_absolute() {
138	        configured
139	    } else {
140	        which::which(binary).unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(binary))
141	    };
142	    let canonical = located.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| located.clone());
143	    let mut read_allowlist = Vec::new();
144	    push_existing_parent_roots(&mut read_allowlist, &located);
145	    push_existing_parent_roots(&mut read_allowlist, &canonical);
146	    if let Ok(canonical_parent) = canonical.parent().unwrap_or(&canonical).canonicalize() {
147	        push_if_exists(&mut read_allowlist, canonical_parent);
148	    }
149	    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) {
150	        for root in [".bun", ".local", ".npm-global", ".opencode"] {
151	            push_if_exists(&mut read_allowlist, home.join(root));
152	        }
153	    }
154	    dedup_paths(&mut read_allowlist);
155	    ResolvedCliBinary {
156	        program: canonical,
157	        read_allowlist,
158	    }
159	}
160	
161	fn cli_provider_write_allowlist(provider: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
162	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
163	        return Vec::new();
164	    };
165	    if let Ok(registry) = ProviderRegistry::builtin()
166	        && let Some(descriptor) = registry.get(provider)
167	    {
168	        let mut paths = descriptor
169	            .sandbox_writes
170	            .iter()
171	            .map(|path| expand_home_path(path, &home))
172	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
173	        dedup_paths(&mut paths);
174	        return paths;
175	    }
176	    let mut paths = Vec::new();
177	    if provider.contains("codex") {
178	        paths.push(home.join(".codex"));
179	    }
180	    if provider.contains("claude") {
181	        paths.push(home.join(".claude"));
182	    }
183	    paths
184	}
185	
186	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path, home: &Path) -> PathBuf {
187	    if path == Path::new("~") {
188	        return home.to_path_buf();
189	    }
190	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
191	        return home.join(rest);
192	    }
193	    path.to_path_buf()
194	}
195	
196	fn push_existing_parent_roots(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>, path: &Path) {
197	    push_if_exists(paths, path);
198	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
199	        push_if_exists(paths, parent);
200	    }
201	    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) {
202	        for root in [".bun", ".local", ".npm-global", ".opencode"] {
203	            let candidate = home.join(root);
204	            if path.starts_with(&candidate) {
205	                push_if_exists(paths, candidate);
206	            }
207	        }
208	    }
209	}
210	
211	fn push_if_exists(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
212	    let path = path.into();
213	    if path.exists() {
214	        paths.push(path);
215	    }
216	}
217	
218	fn dedup_paths(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
219	    paths.sort();
220	    paths.dedup();
221	}

223	pub(crate) async fn write_output(path: Option<&PathBuf>, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
224	    let Some(path) = path else {
225	        return Ok(());
226	    };
227	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
228	        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
229	            .await
230	            .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
231	                path: parent.display().to_string(),
232	                source,
233	            })?;
234	    }
235	    let body = format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr);
236	    tokio::fs::write(path, body)
237	        .await
238	        .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
239	            path: path.display().to_string(),
240	            source,
241	        })
242	}

244	pub(crate) fn ensure_success(provider: &str, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
245	    if output.status_code == Some(0) {
246	        return Ok(());
247	    }
248	    Err(ProviderError::Cli {
249	        provider: provider.to_string(),
250	        detail: format!(
251	            "subprocess exited with {:?}: {}{}",
252	            output.status_code, output.stdout, output.stderr
253	        ),
254	    })
255	}

557	// accumulateMessageTokenUsage rolls up explicit per-message token
558	// metadata into session totals without inferring presence from raw
559	// numeric values alone.
560	func accumulateMessageTokenUsage(
561		sess *ParsedSession,
562		messages []ParsedMessage,
563	) {
564		sess.aggregateTokenPresenceKnown = true
565		for _, m := range messages {
566			if m.HasOutputTokens {
567				sess.HasTotalOutputTokens = true
568				sess.TotalOutputTokens += m.OutputTokens
569			}
570			if m.HasContextTokens {
571				sess.HasPeakContextTokens = true
572				if m.ContextTokens > sess.PeakContextTokens {
573					sess.PeakContextTokens = m.ContextTokens
574				}
575			}
576		}
577	}
578	
579	// InferTokenPresence determines whether context/output tokens were
580	// present in a provider payload. It starts from explicit boolean
581	// flags (and non-zero numeric values), then inspects tokenUsage JSON
582	// keys when available. This is the single source of truth for token
583	// presence inference across all storage backends.
584	func InferTokenPresence(
585		tokenUsage []byte,
586		contextTokens, outputTokens int,
587		hasContext, hasOutput bool,
588	) (bool, bool) {
589		hasContext = hasContext || contextTokens != 0
590		hasOutput = hasOutput || outputTokens != 0
591	
592		if len(tokenUsage) == 0 {
593			return hasContext, hasOutput
594		}
595	
596		var payload map[string]json.RawMessage
597		if err := json.Unmarshal(tokenUsage, &payload); err != nil {
598			return hasContext, hasOutput
599		}
600	
601		for key := range payload {
602			switch key {
603			case "input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens",
604				"cache_read_input_tokens", "input",
605				"cached", "context_tokens":
606				hasContext = true
607			case "output_tokens", "output":
608				hasOutput = true
609			}
610		}
611		return hasContext, hasOutput
612	}
613	
614	// TokenPresence reports whether context/output token fields were
615	// present in the provider payload. Falls back to raw token_usage
616	// key inspection when parser-specific flags were not populated.
617	func (m ParsedMessage) TokenPresence() (bool, bool) {
618		if m.tokenPresenceKnown {
619			return m.HasContextTokens, m.HasOutputTokens
620		}
621		return InferTokenPresence(
622			m.TokenUsage, m.ContextTokens, m.OutputTokens,
623			m.HasContextTokens, m.HasOutputTokens,
624		)
625	}
626	
627	// AggregateTokenPresence reports whether aggregate session token
628	// metrics were present. This preserves explicit flags and falls
629	// back to non-zero aggregates for providers like Kimi that only
630	// expose truthful session-level totals in current Task 1 paths.
631	func (s ParsedSession) AggregateTokenPresence() (bool, bool) {
632		if s.aggregateTokenPresenceKnown {
633			return s.HasTotalOutputTokens, s.HasPeakContextTokens
634		}

## What deadreckon's recent provider commits actually shipped

Three commits formed a tight loop:

- `6bdafe2` — descriptor TOMLs + a `ProviderRegistry` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/registry/mod.rs:122` defines `ProviderDescriptor`)
- `fe0297a` — moved hard-coded defaults (model lists, sandbox paths) into descriptors
- `1af0778` — added `probe_*` for cli/http/local-http and a `dr providers detect` CLI verb

Today only two CLI providers are descriptor-backed: `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex`. JSONL log ingestion (commit `4132e48`) lives in `crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:10861` as a hard-coded `match state.provider.as_deref()` with two arms (`CodexCli`, `ClaudeCode`). Everything beyond detection — log discovery, session matching, message extraction — is bespoke per provider.

## What agentsview already does canonically

Two layers worth stealing from:

1. **`internal/parser/types.go` `Registry`** — 24 agents (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode, OpenHands, Cursor, Amp, Zencoder, iFlow, VSCode-Copilot, Pi, OpenClaw, Kimi, Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Kiro, KiroIDE, Cortex, Hermes, Forge, Piebald, Warp, Positron). Each `AgentDef` declares: `EnvVar`, `ConfigKey`, `DefaultDirs[]`, `IDPrefix`, `WatchSubdirs[]`, `ShallowWatch`, `FileBased`, plus function pointers `DiscoverFunc`/`FindSourceFunc`.
2. **`internal/parser/taxonomy.go` `NormalizeToolCategory`** — single switch that flattens 100+ raw tool names from every agent into 9 canonical categories (Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Grep/Glob/Task/Tool/Other).

Plus normalized `ParsedSession` / `ParsedMessage` / `ParsedToolCall` shapes (`types.go:441–625`) and per-agent JSONL parsers in `internal/parser/{claude,codex,gemini,...}.go`.

## Field-level mapping: descriptor ↔ AgentDef

| agentsview `AgentDef` | deadreckon `ProviderDescriptor` today | gap |
|---|---|---|
| `Type` | `id` | ✅ same concept |
| `DisplayName` | `display_name` | ✅ |
| `EnvVar` | — | **missing** (overrides where to look for sessions) |
| `ConfigKey` | — | n/a (agentsview-specific config plumbing) |
| `DefaultDirs[]` | `fs_detection_paths[]` | partial — descriptor has it but only used to tell users "look here", not for runtime ingest |
| `IDPrefix` | — | **missing** (needed to namespace session IDs once we ingest >1 provider) |
| `WatchSubdirs[]` | — | **missing** (which subtree to fs-watch) |
| `ShallowWatch` | — | **missing** (perf knob: don't recurse) |
| `FileBased` | implied by `kind = cli`/`scripted` | partially derivable |
| `DiscoverFunc` | hard-coded in `provider_jsonl_log_spec` | **needs to be table-driven** |
| `FindSourceFunc` | n/a | future: required if deadreckon ever needs to resume/inspect a single session |
| (no equivalent) | `default_binary`, `version_probe`, `exec_template`, `auth`, `sandbox_*`, `install_hint`, `model_catalog` | deadreckon-specific (it *runs* the agent; agentsview only *parses* it) |

The two registries are complementary, not redundant. agentsview = "after the run, find and parse logs." deadreckon = "before the run, install/launch/sandbox the agent." They share the *identity layer* (id, display name, fs paths, prefix) and diverge after that.

## How to leverage agentsview to grow deadreckon coverage

Three concrete extensions, in priority order:

**1. Extend `ProviderDescriptor` with an `[ingest]` block.** Add the agentsview-side fields so the JSONL streamer in `main.rs:10861` becomes table-driven instead of a 2-arm match:

[ingest]
id_prefix = "codex:"
env_var = "CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR"
default_dirs = [".codex/sessions", ".codex/archived_sessions"]
watch_subdirs = []
shallow_watch = false
schema = "codex-cli"          # picks parser variant
cwd_match = "session-meta"    # vs "top-level" for claude-code

Replace the hard-coded `match` with a lookup against the descriptor. This is a 1-day refactor that immediately unblocks any descriptor that fills in `[ingest]`.

**2. Port `NormalizeToolCategory` verbatim** into `deadreckon-providers` as a free function (`pub fn normalize_tool_category(raw: &str) -> ToolCategory`). **3. ### 5. **Undo / Rollback**

**Undo entry**: `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:9240–9262` (`undo_command`)

Undo relies **only** on deadreckon-internal snapshots, **not** provider logs:
1. Loads `PipelineState` for run
2. Calls `undo_restore_state()` to resolve source path for in-place mode
3. Calls `restore_snapshot()` from codebase file tree
4. Appends trace record `"undo.restore_snapshot"` to `traces.jsonl`

**Snapshot restore** (`deadreckon-core/src/artifacts.rs:82–99`):
```rust
pub fn restore_snapshot(state: &PipelineState, turn: u32) -> Result<()> {
    let snapshot_dir = state.run_root.join("snapshots").join(format!("turn-{turn}"));
    copy_tree(&snapshot_dir, &state.working_dir)
}
```

**Data flow**: Snapshots are taken at each turn (managed by turn loop) and stored in `run_root/snapshots/turn-{N}`. Provider logs (`traces.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `spend.jsonl`) are purely observational; undo does not reference them. **Provider logs would need to plug in only if we wanted to rewind provider-side state** (e.g., API quotas, remote sessions), which is not currently supported.

## Extraction Guide: Agent CLI Discovery & Session Parsing

This guide documents the minimum facts deadreckon needs to discover session files on disk, match them to working directories, and extract per-turn activity for eight well-supported agent CLIs supported by agentsview's parser.

---

### **1. CODEX** (Canonical Reference)

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.codex/sessions/` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`. EnvVar override: `CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR`. (Registry types.go:76-89)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename stem (e.g., `session-abc123.jsonl` → session ID `abc123`, prefixed `codex:` by ParseCodexSession:1175). Fallback: `session_meta` line field `payload.id` (codex.go:122).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Codex uses `session_meta` payload's `cwd` field (early line, always populated first); also extracts git branch from `payload.git.branch` to refine project name via `ExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranch` (codex.go:124-131).

**Per-message shape:** Role (`role`: "user" or "assistant"), content (extracted from `payload.content[].text`), tool calls (`response_item.type=="function_call"` with `name` + `call_id`), tool results (`function_call_output.output`), model (`turn_context.model`), token usage (`event_msg.token_count.info.last_token_usage`), timestamp (`timestamp` ISO8601). (codex.go:88-180)

**Termination detection:** Task lifecycle events (codex.go:185): `task_started`, `task_complete`, `turn_aborted` → termination.go:74-82 maps to `awaiting_user` (task_complete), `tool_call_pending` (task_started), or unknown. Last task event signals state (classifyCodexTermination codex.go:1213-1225).

**Quirks:** Subagent spawning via `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent` calls (codex.go:218-227). Pending agent events cache notifications until matched to a wait call (codex.go:406-418). Token usage deduplication via `lastTokenUsageRaw` (codex.go:198-200). Exec-originated sessions skipped historically (now parsed; IsCodexExecSessionFile codex.go:1102-1125).

---

### **2. CLAUDE** (Claude Code)

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.claude/projects/`. EnvVar: `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR`. Each project dir → multiple `*.jsonl` session files. (Registry types.go:65-75)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename stem (e.g., `abc123.jsonl` → sessionId `abc123`, no prefix for Claude). Early entries carry `sessionId` field; file derivation used when absent (claude.go:68, 197-205).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Top-level `cwd` field on first user entry (claude.go:187). Also tracks `gitBranch` for project refinement. Session metadata stored in claudeSessionMeta (claude.go:618-635).

**Per-message shape:** Role (`type`: "user" or "assistant"), content (parsed from `message.content[]` array of blocks—text, tool_use, tool_result), tool calls (content block `type=="tool_use"` with `id`, `name`, `input`), tool results (`type=="tool_result"` with `tool_use_id`), model (`message.model`), token usage (`message.usage`), stop reason (`message.stop_reason`), timestamp (`timestamp`). (claude.go:536-610, 1376-1401)

**Termination detection:** Claude.stop_reason vocabulary (Classify termination.go:45-69): `end_turn` → awaiting_user, or orphaned tool_use (hasOrphanedToolCall termination.go:90-121). File truncation detection via invalid JSON on last line without newline (claude.go:237-240).

**Quirks:** DAG-aware fork detection (uuid/parentUuid chains; claude.go:682-850). Large-gap forks (>3 user turns) split into separate sessions with `-<uuid>` suffix. Assistant message chunk merging for same-message.id within a turn (claude.go:1003-1078). Queued_command attachments (user messages typed mid-tool-call) merged by timestamp (claude.go:895-934). Compact summary boundaries marked (claude.go:510-527).

---

### **3. GEMINI**

**Storage shape:** JSON (single file per session) or JSONL. Default: `~/.gemini/tmp/`. EnvVar: `GEMINI_DIR`. Single session → one `*.json` file or JSONL stream. (Registry types.go:102-113)

**Session ID extraction:** Top-level `sessionId` field mandatory (gemini.go:77-82). No prefix.

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Project extracted from environment context; no cwd in transcripts (gemini.go:72-100). Project defaults to "gemini" when absent.

**Per-message shape:** Role (`type`: "user" or "gemini" for assistant), content (text in `content` field or content blocks array), tool calls (within `toolCalls[]` array: `id`, `name`, `args`), tool results embedded in `toolCalls[].result[].functionResponse`), model (`model` field), token usage (`tokens` object: `input`, `output`, `cached`), timestamp (`timestamp` ISO8601). (gemini.go:40-100+)

**Termination detection:** Last message's role; no explicit stop_reason vocabulary. Classify via orphaned tool calls (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Dual format support (JSON object vs. JSONL stream in same file). Thought blocks captured separately (Gemini's reasoning traces). Tool results inline in tool call definition rather than separate messages.

---

### **4. OPENCODE** (Dual Storage Modes)

**Storage shape:** Two modes detected by ResolveOpenCodeSource (discovery.go:75-110):
  - **File-based:** `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/<project>/*.json` (multiple projects, each with multiple sessions).
  - **SQLite legacy:** `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (single file, query-based).
  EnvVar: `OPENCODE_DIR`. Watch roots computed in ResolveOpenCodeWatchRoots (discovery.go:250-269).

**Session ID extraction:** File mode: filename stem `sessionid.json` (discovery.go:225-235). SQLite mode: `session.id` column query (opencode.go:42-60). Virtual path format for DB: `dbpath#sessionid` (discovery.go:271-275).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** File mode: `directory` field in JSON (opencode.go:292-300). Project from directory path or directory field via ExtractProjectFromCwd.

**Per-message shape:** File-based sessions stored as aggregated JSON. Messages extracted by query; role, content, tool data format TBD from opencode.go parser (reading first 100 lines shows sqlite/file mode dispatch but message structure deferred to later code).

**Termination detection:** SQLite: `time_updated` tracks last activity (opencode.go:88-100). File mode: relies on standard orphaned-tool logic (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Hybrid roots (storage/ + opencode.db coexist): storage canonical, SQLite fallback (discovery.go:206-239). Subdir watch path expansion (message/, part/ subdirs created lazily; discovery.go:121-126). Virtual path encoding for SQLite sessions.

---

### **5. AMP**

**Storage shape:** JSON (one thread per file). Default: `~/.local/share/amp/threads/`. EnvVar: `AMP_DIR`. Filename pattern: `T-*.json` (thread files). (Registry types.go:154-163)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename-derived ID (ampThreadIDFromPath amp.go:39). Fallback: JSON `id` field validated by isValidAmpThreadID (amp.go:42).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Project extracted from `env.initial.trees[0].displayName` (amp.go:75). No cwd in transcripts.

**Per-message shape:** Meta structure at `meta.traces[]` with traces containing `type` (Message, Action, Observation), `timestamp` (string), content in trace-specific fields. Token usage in metadata, model from trace context. Title as first message (amp.go:80+).

**Termination detection:** End time from last trace with non-empty `endTime` (amp.go:61-72). Classify via message count and last message type.

**Quirks:** Nested metadata structure (traces within meta). Thread lifecycle tracked via created (epoch ms) and endTime. Tree/project nesting in env context.

---

### **6. OPENHANDS**

**Storage shape:** Directory-per-session (UUID directory names). Default: `~/.openhands/conversations/`. EnvVar: `OPENHANDS_CONVERSATIONS_DIR`. Each session → directory with conversation files inside. (Registry types.go:131-141)

**Session ID extraction:** Directory name (validated by IsValidSessionID, discovery.go:35-36). Stored as UUID; discoverer finds directories matching UUID pattern (openhands.go:25-54).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Working directory stored in session metadata within conversation files; extraction deferred to parser.

**Per-message shape:** Message events identified by `type=="MessageEvent"` (openhands.go:18-20). Content, role (MessageEvent.role), timestamps in event entries. Tool use/result in ActionEvent/ObservationEvent (openhands.go:19-20).

**Termination detection:** Last event type determines state (MessageEvent vs. ActionEvent vs. ObservationEvent).

**Quirks:** Session as directory (not single file). Multiple file types (event log structure). Shallow watch (ShallowWatch=true Registry:138); relies on periodic sync for nested discovery.

---

### **7. IFLOW**

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.iflow/projects/`. EnvVar: `IFLOW_DIR`. Filename pattern: `session-*.jsonl`. (Registry types.go:176-185)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename: `session-<uuid>.jsonl` → trim prefix, then prepend `iflow:` (iflow.go:32-47).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Top-level `cwd` field on entries (analogous to Claude, iflow.go:55-80).

**Per-message shape:** Similar to Claude: `type` (user/assistant), `message.content[]` blocks (text, tool_use, tool_result), uuid/parentUuid DAG structure, timestamps. Tool calls in content blocks (iflow.go:18-25).

**Termination detection:** uuid/parentUuid chain forms streaming snapshots, not forks—no fork splitting applied (iflow.go:27-31). Termination via lastTaskEvent or orphaned tools.

**Quirks:** DAG structure is sliding-window snapshot stream, not conversation forks—parse linearly without fork detection. Similar message structure to Claude but different semantic interpretation of uuid chains.

---

### **8. COPILOT**

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.copilot/session-state/`. EnvVar: `COPILOT_DIR`. WatchSubdirs: `["session-state"]`. (Registry types.go:91-101)

**Session ID extraction:** JSONL `type==session.start` event carries `data.sessionId` (copilot.go:54-70, 75-76).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Session start event's `data.context.cwd` + `context.branch` (copilot.go:79-80).

**Per-message shape:** Event-based: `type` determines message type (user.message, assistant.message, tool.execution_complete, assistant.reasoning, session.model_change). Role implicit in event type. Content in `data` object. Tool calls/results in tool.execution_complete events (copilot.go:13-21, 42-70).

**Termination detection:** Model from session.model_change; last event type signals state. Orphaned tools via standard logic (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Event-stream format (not message-centric). Session lifecycle marked by session.start event. Tool execution as discrete events, not message-embedded blocks.

---

### **Shared Infrastructure**

**linereader.go** (Line-by-line JSONL parsing): newLineReader manages buffered scanning with a configurable max line size (64MB) and graceful oversized-line skipping. readJSONLFrom enables offset-based resume for incremental parsing (linereader.go:37-160). Used by all JSONL parsers (Codex, Claude, iFlow, Copilot).

**timestamp.go** (Uniform timestamp parsing): parseTimestamp tries eight ISO8601 variants in priority order (RFC3339Nano, RFC3339, milliseconds, zone variants, space-separated) to accommodate agent diversity (timestamp.go:10-32). Used across all agents; logParseError flags unparseable strings.

**termination.go** (Unified termination classification): Classify function (termination.go:45-69) maps message sequence + stop_reason + file truncation → TerminationStatus enum (awaiting_user, clean, tool_call_pending, truncated). isAwaitingUserStopReason (termination.go:75-82) unifies agent vocabularies (Claude "end_turn", Codex "task_complete"). hasOrphanedToolCall (termination.go:90-121) detects unresolved tool_use blocks after last assistant message.

**discovery.go** (Session file discovery & location): DiscoverFunc/FindSourceFunc pairs (Registry AgentDef types.go:52-59) handle agent-specific filesystem layout. UUID regex uuidRe (discovery.go:20-24) matches session identifiers. ResolveOpenCodeSource (discovery.go:75-110) dual-mode detection. Helper isDirOrSymlink (discovery.go:29-45) normalizes directory checks. ExtractProjectFromCwd/NormalizeName infer project names from filesystem paths.

**taxonomy.go** (Tool normalization): NormalizeToolCategory (taxonomy.go:8-206) is the **single source of truth** for raw tool name → canonical category mapping across all agents (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Task, Tool, Other). Agents emit names like "shell_command" (Codex), "run_command" (Gemini), "bash" (OpenCode), "Shell" (Cursor) → all map to "Bash". Subagent detection via substring match (line 201) captures MCP-prefixed tools and spawn_subagent naming patterns.

---

**Summary:** Deadreckon can implement per-agent discovery and parsing by adopting agentsview's Registry pattern (agent type → storage dirs → discovery func → parse func), reusing timestamp and termination logic, and mapping raw tool names through NormalizeToolCategory. The dual-mode OpenCode strategy (file vs. SQLite) and Claude's DAG fork splitting represent the most complex behaviors; other agents follow more linear parsing paths. Each agent's session_meta carries cwd; combined with git branch metadata, this enables robust working-directory attribution.

376	// StripHostPrefix splits a remote session ID into its host
377	// and raw ID parts. Remote IDs use the form "host~rawID"
378	// where the "~" separator avoids conflict with both agent
379	// prefixes (":") and URL path segments ("/"). For local
380	// session IDs (no "~" present), host is empty and rawID is
381	// the original ID.
382	func StripHostPrefix(id string) (host, rawID string) {
383		if before, after, ok := strings.Cut(id, "~"); ok {
384			return before, after
385		}
386		return "", id
387	}

---

## DESIGN DOC: Deadreckon Provider CLI Log Parsing & Consumer Surfaces

### Section 1: Undo / Rollback Behavior

**Implementation Location:** `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/artifacts.rs:66–99`, `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:9240–9281`

Undo in deadreckon restores **filesystem snapshots only**—it does not read or truncate provider JSONL logs. The mechanism is:

1. **Data restored:** Filesystem state from per-turn snapshots stored in `run_root/snapshots/turn-N/` (copied via `copy_tree()` at `artifacts.rs:78`). The `snapshot_working()` function (line 66) creates a full recursive filesystem copy at each turn boundary; `restore_snapshot()` (line 82) reverses this by deleting the current working_dir and copying the snapshot back.

2. **Provider log involvement:** None. The undo command (`undo_command()` at `main.rs:9240`) invokes `restore_snapshot()` with a target turn and appends a trace event (`"undo.restore_snapshot"` at line 9255). It does not parse, read, or truncate codex/claude JSONL logs. Provider logs remain untouched in their source directories (`~/.codex/sessions/` or `~/.claude/projects/`).

3. **Artifacts truncated:** After undo, the runtime truncates deadreckon-owned JSONL files—specifically `traces.jsonl` and `spend.jsonl`—via `truncate_run_artifacts_after_turn()` at `turn_loop.rs:1099–1121`. This function filters each file to keep only entries with `turn <= from_turn` (line 1136), then deletes filesystem snapshots beyond the target turn (lines 1107–1118). `events.jsonl` is **not** truncated; provider logs are **not** touched.

4. **Seam for multi-provider truncation:** To extend undo to truncate a provider JSONL (e.g., to re-run from a specific Claude Code session turn), the seam would be in `truncate_run_artifacts_after_turn()` at `turn_loop.rs:1100`. Currently it hardcodes `["traces.jsonl", "spend.jsonl"]`; adding provider log paths and a turn-aware filter (similar to `truncate_jsonl_after_turn()` at line 1123) would truncate provider sessions. However, provider logs use **turn IDs are not fields**—they are keyed by session timestamp and message UUID. A mapping from deadreckon turn → provider turn/message UUID would be required, likely stored in `provenance.jsonl` (which records `prompt_id: "turn-N"`, `tool_call_id`, and `session_id` at `artifacts.rs:30–38`).

---

### Section 2: TUI Provider Activity Feed

**Location:** `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:10545–11239`, displayed at `main.rs:11764`

The provider activity feed (`provider_activity: Vec<String>` on `AttachLive`, line 10545) extracts **free-form human-readable log lines** from provider JSONL files and displays them in reverse chronological order in the `attach` TUI panel.

**Codex Activity Extractor** (`codex_activity_line()`, lines 11071–11124):
```rust
fn codex_activity_line(line: &str, activity: &mut ProviderActivity) -> Option<String> {
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(line).ok()?;
    let timestamp = short_timestamp(value.get("timestamp").and_then(Value::as_str));
    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
    match (
        value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str),
        payload.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str),
    ) {
        (Some("event_msg"), Some("task_started")) => Some(format!("{timestamp} codex started")),
        (Some("event_msg"), Some("agent_message")) => payload
            .get("message")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .map(|message| format!("{timestamp} agent {}", one_line(message, 140))),
        (Some("event_msg"), Some("token_count")) => {
            let usage = payload.get("info")?.get("total_token_usage")?;
            let total = usage.get("total_tokens").and_then(Value::as_u64)?;
            let window = payload
                .get("info")
                .and_then(|info| info.get("model_context_window"))
                .and_then(Value::as_u64)
                .unwrap_or(0);
            activity.context_tokens = Some(total);
            activity.context_window = Some(window);
            let rate = payload
                .get("rate_limits")
                .and_then(|limits| limits.get("primary"))
                .and_then(|primary| primary.get("used_percent"))
                .and_then(Value::as_f64)
                .unwrap_or(0.0);
            Some(format!(
                "{timestamp} tokens {total}/{window} rate {rate:.0}%"
            ))
        }
        (Some("response_item"), Some("function_call")) => {
            let name = payload
                .get("name")
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or("tool");
            let args = payload
                .get("arguments")
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or("");
            Some(format!(
                "{timestamp} tool {name} {}",
                one_line(&tool_call_summary(name, args), 140)
            ))
        }
        (Some("response_item"), Some("function_call_output")) => payload
            .get("output")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .map(|output| format!("{timestamp} result {}", one_line(output, 140))),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

Codex extracts: `task_started` (empty), `agent_message` (truncated to 140 chars), `token_count` (with rate limits), function_call (tool name + args), and function_call_output. Context tokens and window are also populated into `activity.context_tokens/window`.

**Claude Activity Extractor** (`claude_activity_lines()`, lines 11126–11139 dispatching to helper functions):
```rust
fn claude_activity_lines(line: &str, activity: &mut ProviderActivity) -> Vec<String> {
    let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let timestamp = short_timestamp(value.get("timestamp").and_then(Value::as_str));
    let row_type = value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    match row_type {
        "assistant" => claude_assistant_activity_lines(&value, &timestamp, activity),
        "user" => claude_user_activity_lines(&value, &timestamp),
        "attachment" => claude_attachment_activity_line(&value, &timestamp)
            .into_iter()
            .collect(),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}
```

For `"assistant"` rows (lines 11142–11188): extracts `message.content[]` parts—text nodes (→ `"agent"`), thinking nodes (→ `"thinking"`), and tool_use (→ `"tool {name}"`). Also populates `activity.context_tokens` from `message.usage`. For `"user"` rows (lines 11190–11219): filters `message.content[]` for `tool_result` parts and formats as `"result"` or `"error"` prefix. For `"attachment"` rows (lines 11221–11239): matches `type == "todo_reminder"` and outputs `"todo {completed}/{total} done {active} active"`.

**Display Contract:** Each line is a **free-form string**, no structured container. Lines are collected into `provider_activity.lines` (a `Vec<String>`), then displayed in the TUI at `main.rs:11764` via `lines.extend(live.provider_activity.iter().rev().cloned())` within `attach_activity_lines()`. They render in the `"Activity"` panel with other deadreckon artifacts (spend, traces, events).

**240-Entry Cap & Reversal** (lines 10962–10973):
```rust
fn cap_provider_activity(mut activity: ProviderActivity, cap: usize) -> ProviderActivity {
    activity.lines = activity
        .lines
        .into_iter()
        .rev()
        .take(cap)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .into_iter()
        .rev()
        .collect();
    activity
}
```

The cap is applied after parsing one JSONL file. It reverse→take(240)→reverse, which keeps the **latest 240 events** in chronological order. Rationale: JSONL files grow unbounded as sessions run; 240 truncates the feed to prevent TUI lag and memory bloat while preserving the most recent activity for debugging. The double-reversal ensures old events are dropped from the head, new ones from the tail.

**Provider Log Truncation:** Unlike `traces.jsonl` and `spend.jsonl`, provider JSONL files (in `~/.codex/sessions/` or `~/.claude/projects/`) are **never truncated by deadreckon**. Users must manually delete provider log files or sessions if they want to reclaim disk. This is intentional—provider logs are read-only imports; deadreckon does not own them.

    let provider = &json["providers"][0];

    let ping = deadreckon(temp.path())

        .expect("detect ping");
    assert_success(&ping);
    let json: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&ping.stdout).expect("json ping");
    let provider = &json["providers"][0];

fn repo_tempdir() -> TempDir {
    let root = Path::new("/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.test-tmp");

    fs::create_dir_all(temp.path().join("empty-bin")).expect("empty bin");
    temp
}

fn deadreckon(home: &Path) -> Command {
    let mut command = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_deadreckon"));
    command.env("DEADRECKON_HOME", home).env("NO_COLOR", "1");
    command
}

fn write_provider_override(home: &Path, name: &str, body: &str) {
    let dir = home.join("providers.d");
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("providers.d");
    fs::write(dir.join(name), body).expect("write provider override");
}

fn write_fake_binary(dir: &Path, name: &str, version: &str) {
    fs::create_dir_all(dir).expect("bin dir");
    let path = dir.join(name);
    fs::write(
        &path,
        format!(
            "#!/bin/sh\nprintf '%s\\n' '{}'\n",
            version.replace('\'', "'\\''")
        ),
    )
    .expect("fake binary");
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let mut permissions = fs::metadata(&path).expect("metadata").permissions();
        permissions.set_mode(0o755);
        fs::set_permissions(&path, permissions).expect("chmod");
    }
}

fn assert_success(output: &std::process::Output) {
    assert!(
        output.status.success(),
        "stdout:\n{}\nstderr:\n{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
    );
}

230	// applyCodexTokenUsage normalizes Codex token usage fields
231	// into the Anthropic-style shape expected by the usage and cost
232	// queries. Codex reports input_tokens as the full input count
233	// (cached portion included), while the downstream cost formula
234	// treats input_tokens as the uncached remainder and bills
235	// cache_read_input_tokens separately. Subtracting cached here
236	// prevents double-counting the cached portion at the full input
237	// rate.
238	//
239	//	input_tokens - cached_input_tokens → input_tokens  (uncached)
240	//	output_tokens                      → output_tokens
241	//	cached_input_tokens                → cache_read_input_tokens
242	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) applyCodexTokenUsage(
243		msg *ParsedMessage, raw string,
244	) {
245		usage := gjson.Parse(raw)
246		totalInput := int(usage.Get("input_tokens").Int())
247		cached := int(usage.Get("cached_input_tokens").Int())
248		output := int(usage.Get("output_tokens").Int())
249	
250		uncached := max(totalInput-cached, 0)
251	
252		normalized := map[string]int{
253			"input_tokens":            uncached,
254			"output_tokens":           output,
255			"cache_read_input_tokens": cached,
256		}
257		j, err := json.Marshal(normalized)
258		if err != nil {
259			return
260		}
261		msg.TokenUsage = j
262		msg.OutputTokens = output
263		msg.HasOutputTokens = output > 0
264		msg.ContextTokens = uncached + cached
265		msg.HasContextTokens = totalInput > 0 || cached > 0
266	}

352					ToolUseID:         callID,
353					AgentID:           agentID,
354					SubagentSessionID: codexSubagentSessionID(agentID),
355					Source:            "wait_output",
356					Status:            statusName,
357					Content:           text,
358					Timestamp:         ts,
359				})
360				return true
361			})
362		}
363	}
364	
365	// setCallSubagentSessionID links a tool call to the session of
366	// the subagent it spawned. Callers must invoke this only after
367	// the originating function_call has been processed (which
368	// populates b.callRefs[callID]); otherwise the link is silently
369	// dropped. In real codex session files the spawn function_call
370	// always precedes both its function_call_output and the
371	// collab_agent_spawn_end event_msg.
372	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) setCallSubagentSessionID(
373		callID, sessionID string,
374	) {
375		if callID == "" || sessionID == "" {
376			return
377		}
378		ref, ok := b.callRefs[callID]
379		if !ok || ref.messageIndex < 0 || ref.messageIndex >= len(b.messages) {
380			return
381		}
382		if ref.callIndex < 0 || ref.callIndex >= len(b.messages[ref.messageIndex].ToolCalls) {
383			return
384		}
385		b.messages[ref.messageIndex].ToolCalls[ref.callIndex].SubagentSessionID = sessionID
386	}
387	
388	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) handleSubagentNotification(
389		content string, ts time.Time,
390	) bool {
391		agentID, statusName, text := parseCodexSubagentNotification(content)
392		if agentID == "" || text == "" {
393			return false
394		}
395		if callID := b.agentWaitCalls[agentID]; callID != "" {
396			b.appendCallResultEvent(callID, ParsedToolResultEvent{
397				AgentID:           agentID,
398				SubagentSessionID: codexSubagentSessionID(agentID),
399				Source:            "subagent_notification",
400				Status:            statusName,
401				Content:           text,
402				Timestamp:         ts,
403			})
404			return true
405		}
406	
407		b.pendingAgentEvents[agentID] = append(
408			b.pendingAgentEvents[agentID], codexPendingEvent{
409				agentID:   agentID,
410				source:    "subagent_notification",
411				status:    statusName,
412				text:      text,
413				timestamp: ts,
414				ordinal:   b.ordinal,
415			},
416		)
417		b.ordinal++
418		return true
419	}
420	
421	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) appendCallResultEvent(
422		callID string, ev ParsedToolResultEvent,
423	) {
424		if callID == "" {
425			return
426		}
427		ref, ok := b.callRefs[callID]
428		if !ok || ref.messageIndex < 0 || ref.messageIndex >= len(b.messages) {
429			return
430		}
431		if ref.callIndex < 0 || ref.callIndex >= len(b.messages[ref.messageIndex].ToolCalls) {
432			return
433		}
434		tc := &b.messages[ref.messageIndex].ToolCalls[ref.callIndex]
435		if ev.ToolUseID == "" {
436			ev.ToolUseID = tc.ToolUseID
437		}
438		if ev.SubagentSessionID == "" && ev.AgentID != "" {
439			ev.SubagentSessionID = codexSubagentSessionID(ev.AgentID)
440		}
441		if b.hasEquivalentCallResultEvent(tc.ResultEvents, ev) {
442			return
443		}
444		tc.ResultEvents = append(tc.ResultEvents, ev)
445	}
446	
447	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) hasEquivalentCallResultEvent(
448		events []ParsedToolResultEvent, candidate ParsedToolResultEvent,
449	) bool {
450		for _, existing := range events {
451			if existing.AgentID == candidate.AgentID &&
452				existing.Status == candidate.Status &&
453				existing.Content == candidate.Content {
454				return true
455			}
456		}
457		return false
458	}
459	
460	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) claimPendingAgentEvents(
461		callID, agentID string,
462	) {
463		pending := b.pendingAgentEvents[agentID]
464		if len(pending) == 0 {
465			return
466		}
467		for _, ev := range pending {
468			b.appendCallResultEvent(callID, ParsedToolResultEvent{
469				AgentID:           ev.agentID,
470				SubagentSessionID: codexSubagentSessionID(ev.agentID),
471				Source:            ev.source,
472				Status:            ev.status,
473				Content:           ev.text,
474				Timestamp:         ev.timestamp,
475			})
476		}
477		delete(b.pendingAgentEvents, agentID)
478	}
479	
480	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) flushPendingAgentResults() {
481		if len(b.pendingAgentEvents) == 0 {
482			return
483		}
484		agentIDs := make([]string, 0, len(b.pendingAgentEvents))
485		for agentID := range b.pendingAgentEvents {
486			agentIDs = append(agentIDs, agentID)
487		}
488		sort.Strings(agentIDs)
489		for _, agentID := range agentIDs {
490			pending := b.pendingAgentEvents[agentID]
491			switch {
492			case b.agentWaitCalls[agentID] != "":
493				b.claimPendingAgentEvents(b.agentWaitCalls[agentID], agentID)
494			case b.agentSpawnCalls[agentID] != "":
495				b.claimPendingAgentEvents(b.agentSpawnCalls[agentID], agentID)
496			default:
497				for _, ev := range pending {
498					key := agentID + "\x00" + ev.status + "\x00" + ev.text
499					if _, ok := b.orphanNotificationIx[key]; ok {
500						continue
501					}
502					idx := b.insertMessage(ParsedMessage{
503						Ordinal:       ev.ordinal,
504						Role:          RoleUser,
505						Content:       ev.text,
506						Timestamp:     ev.timestamp,
507						Model:         b.currentModel,
508						ContentLength: len(ev.text),
509					})
510					b.orphanNotificationIx[key] = idx
511				}
512				delete(b.pendingAgentEvents, agentID)
513			}
514		}
515	}
516	
517	func codexSubagentSessionID(agentID string) string {
518		agentID = strings.TrimSpace(agentID)
519		if agentID == "" {
520			return ""
521		}
522		if strings.HasPrefix(agentID, "codex:") {
523			return agentID
524		}
525		return "codex:" + agentID
526	}
527	
528	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) normalizeOrdinals() {
529		sort.SliceStable(b.messages, func(i, j int) bool {
530			if b.messages[i].Ordinal == b.messages[j].Ordinal {
531				return i < j
532			}
533			return b.messages[i].Ordinal < b.messages[j].Ordinal
534		})
535		for i := range b.messages {
536			b.messages[i].Ordinal = i
537		}
538	}
539	
540	func (b *codexSessionBuilder) insertMessage(msg ParsedMessage) int {
541		idx := len(b.messages)
542		for i, existing := range b.messages {
543			if existing.Ordinal > msg.Ordinal ||
544				(existing.Ordinal == msg.Ordinal &&
545					!msg.Timestamp.IsZero() &&
546					(existing.Timestamp.IsZero() ||
547						msg.Timestamp.Before(existing.Timestamp))) {
548				idx = i
549				break
550			}
551		}
552		b.messages = append(b.messages, ParsedMessage{})
553		copy(b.messages[idx+1:], b.messages[idx:])
554		b.messages[idx] = msg
555		for callID, ref := range b.callRefs {
556			if ref.messageIndex >= idx {
557				ref.messageIndex++
558				b.callRefs[callID] = ref
559			}
560		}
561		return idx
562	}
563	
564	func formatCodexFunctionCall(
565		name string, payload gjson.Result,
566	) string {
567		summary := sanitizeToolLabel(payload.Get("summary").Str)
568		args, rawArgs := parseCodexFunctionArgs(payload)
569	
570		switch name {
571		case "exec_command", "shell_command", "shell":
572			return formatCodexBashCall(summary, args, rawArgs)
573		case "write_stdin":
574			return formatCodexWriteStdinCall(summary, args, rawArgs)
575		case "apply_patch":
576			return formatCodexApplyPatchCall(summary, args, rawArgs)
577		case "spawn_agent":
578			return formatCodexSpawnAgentCall(summary, args, rawArgs)
579		}
580	
581		category := NormalizeToolCategory(name)
582		if category == "Other" {
583			header := formatToolHeader("Tool", name)
584			if summary != "" {
585				return header + "\n" + summary
586			}
587			if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" {
588				return header + "\n" + preview
589			}
590			return header
591		}
592	
593		detail := firstNonEmpty(summary,
594			codexCategoryDetail(category, args))
595		header := formatToolHeader(category, detail)
596		if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" {
597			return header + "\n" + preview
598		}
599		return header
600	}
601	
602	func parseCodexFunctionArgs(
603		payload gjson.Result,
604	) (gjson.Result, string) {
605		for _, key := range []string{"arguments", "input"} {
606			arg := payload.Get(key)
607			if !arg.Exists() {
608				continue
609			}
610	
611			switch arg.Type {
612			case gjson.String:
613				s := strings.TrimSpace(arg.Str)
614				if s == "" {
615					continue
616				}
617				if gjson.Valid(s) {
618					return gjson.Parse(s), ""
619				}
620				return gjson.Result{}, s
621			default:
622				if arg.IsObject() {
623					if len(arg.Map()) == 0 {
624						continue
625					}
626					return arg, ""
627				}
628				if arg.IsArray() {
629					if len(arg.Array()) == 0 {
630						continue
631					}
632					return arg, ""
633				}
634				raw := strings.TrimSpace(arg.Raw)
635				if raw == "" {
636					continue
637				}
638				if gjson.Valid(raw) {
639					return gjson.Parse(raw), ""
640				}
641				return gjson.Result{}, raw
642			}
643		}
644		return gjson.Result{}, ""
645	}
646	
647	// extractCodexInputJSON returns the raw JSON string of the
648	// function call arguments from the payload. It checks
649	// "arguments" then "input", normalizing string-encoded JSON
650	// to an object string.
651	func extractCodexInputJSON(payload gjson.Result) string {
652		for _, key := range []string{"arguments", "input"} {
653			arg := payload.Get(key)
654			if !arg.Exists() {
655				continue
656			}
657	
658			switch arg.Type {
659			case gjson.String:
660				s := strings.TrimSpace(arg.Str)
661				if s == "" {
662					continue
663				}
664				if gjson.Valid(s) {
665					if s == "{}" || s == "[]" {
666						continue
667					}
668					return s
669				}
670				return arg.Str
671			default:
672				raw := strings.TrimSpace(arg.Raw)
673				if raw == "" || raw == "{}" || raw == "[]" {
674					continue
675				}
676				return arg.Raw
677			}
678		}
679		return ""
680	}
681	
682	func formatCodexBashCall(
683		summary string, args gjson.Result, rawArgs string,
684	) string {
685		cmd := codexArgValue(args, "cmd", "command")
686		if cmd == "" && rawArgs != "" && !gjson.Valid(rawArgs) {
687			cmd = rawArgs
688		}
689		if cmd == "" && args.Type == gjson.String {
690			cmd = strings.TrimSpace(args.Str)
691		}
692	
693		header := formatToolHeader("Bash", summary)
694		if cmd != "" {
695			firstLine, _, hasMore := strings.Cut(cmd, "\n")
696			if hasMore {
697				return header + "\n$ " + firstLine
698			}
699			return header + "\n$ " + cmd
700		}
701		if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" {
702			return header + "\n" + preview
703		}
704		return header
705	}
706	
707	func formatCodexWriteStdinCall(
708		summary string, args gjson.Result, rawArgs string,
709	) string {
710		if summary == "" {
711			if sid := codexArgValue(args, "session_id"); sid != "" {
712				summary = "stdin -> " + sid
713			} else {
714				summary = "stdin"
715			}
716		}
717	
718		header := formatToolHeader("Bash", summary)
719		chars := codexArgString(args, "chars")
720		if chars != "" {
721			quoted := strings.Trim(
722				strconv.QuoteToASCII(chars), "\"",
723			)
724			return header + "\n" + truncate(quoted, 220)
725		}
726	
727		if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" {
728			return header + "\n" + preview
729		}
730		return header
731	}
732	
733	func formatCodexApplyPatchCall(
734		summary string, args gjson.Result, rawArgs string,
735	) string {
736		patch := codexArgString(args, "patch")
737		if patch == "" && strings.Contains(rawArgs, "*** Begin Patch") {
738			patch = rawArgs
739		}
740	
741		files := extractPatchedFiles(patch)
742		if summary == "" {
743			summary = summarizePatchedFiles(files)
744		}
745	
746		header := formatToolHeader("Edit", summary)
747		if len(files) > 1 {
748			limit := min(len(files), 6)
749			body := strings.Join(files[:limit], "\n")
750			if len(files) > limit {
751				body += fmt.Sprintf("\n+%d more files", len(files)-limit)
752			}
753			return header + "\n" + body
754		}
755		if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" &&
756			len(files) == 0 {
757			return header + "\n" + preview
758		}
759		return header
760	}
761	
762	func formatCodexSpawnAgentCall(
763		summary string, args gjson.Result, rawArgs string,
764	) string {
765		if summary == "" {
766			summary = firstNonEmpty(
767				codexArgValue(args, "agent_type"),
768				codexArgValue(args, "subagent_type"),
769				"spawn_agent",
770			)
771		}
772	
773		header := formatToolHeader("Task", summary)
774		prompt := firstNonEmpty(
775			codexArgValue(args, "description"),
776			codexArgValue(args, "message"),
777			codexArgValue(args, "prompt"),
778		)
779		if prompt != "" {
780			firstLine, _, _ := strings.Cut(prompt, "\n")
781			return header + "\n" + truncate(firstLine, 220)
782		}
783		if preview := codexArgPreview(args, rawArgs); preview != "" {
784			return header + "\n" + preview
785		}
786		return header
787	}
788	
789	func extractPatchedFiles(patch string) []string {
790		if patch == "" {
791			return nil
792		}
793	
794		var files []string
795		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
796		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(patch, "\n") {
797			for _, prefix := range []string{
798				"*** Add File: ",
799				"*** Update File: ",
800				"*** Delete File: ",
801				"*** Move to: ",
802			} {
803				if !strings.HasPrefix(line, prefix) {
804					continue
805				}
806				file := strings.TrimSpace(
807					strings.TrimPrefix(line, prefix),
808				)
809				if file == "" {
810					continue
811				}
812				if _, ok := seen[file]; ok {
813					continue
814				}
815				seen[file] = struct{}{}
816				files = append(files, file)
817				break
818			}
819		}
820		return files
821	}
822	
823	func summarizePatchedFiles(files []string) string {
824		switch len(files) {
825		case 0:
826			return ""
827		case 1:
828			return files[0]
829		default:
830			return fmt.Sprintf(
831				"%s (+%d more)",
832				files[0], len(files)-1,
833			)
834		}
835	}
836	
837	func codexCategoryDetail(
838		category string, args gjson.Result,
839	) string {
840		switch category {
841		case "Read", "Write", "Edit":
842			return codexArgValue(args, "file_path", "path")
843		case "Grep":
844			return codexArgValue(args, "pattern")
845		case "Glob":
846			pattern := codexArgValue(args, "pattern")
847			path := codexArgValue(args, "path")
848			if pattern != "" && path != "" {
849				return fmt.Sprintf("%s in %s", pattern, path)
850			}
851			return firstNonEmpty(pattern, path)
852		case "Task", "Agent":
853			desc := codexArgValue(args, "description")
854			agent := codexArgValue(args, "subagent_type")
855			if desc != "" && agent != "" {
856				return fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", desc, agent)
857			}
858			return firstNonEmpty(desc, agent)
859		default:
860			return ""
861		}
862	}
863	
864	func codexArgString(
865		args gjson.Result, path string,
866	) string {
867		v := args.Get(path)
868		if !v.Exists() {
869			return ""
870		}
871		if v.Type == gjson.String {
872			return v.Str
873		}
874		raw := strings.TrimSpace(v.Raw)
875		if raw == "" || raw == "null" {
876			return ""
877		}
878		return raw
879	}
880	
881	func codexArgValue(
882		args gjson.Result, paths ...string,
883	) string {
884		for _, path := range paths {
885			v := strings.TrimSpace(codexArgString(args, path))
886			if v != "" {
887				return v
888			}
889		}
890		return ""
891	}
892	
893	func codexArgPreview(
894		args gjson.Result, rawArgs string,
895	) string {
896		if rawArgs != "" {
897			flat := strings.Join(
898				strings.Fields(rawArgs), " ",
899			)
900			return truncate(flat, 220)
901		}
902		if args.Exists() {
903			flat := strings.Join(
904				strings.Fields(args.Raw), " ",
905			)
906			if flat != "" {
907				return truncate(flat, 220)
908			}
909		}
910		return ""
911	}
912	
913	func formatToolHeader(
914		label, detail string,
915	) string {
916		label = sanitizeToolLabel(label)
917		if label == "" {
918			label = "Tool"
919		}
920		detail = sanitizeToolLabel(detail)
921		if detail != "" {
922			return fmt.Sprintf("[%s: %s]", label, detail)
923		}
924		return fmt.Sprintf("[%s]", label)
925	}
926	
927	func sanitizeToolLabel(s string) string {
928		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
929		if s == "" {
930			return ""
931		}
932		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "]", ")")
933		return strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ")
934	}
935	
936	func firstNonEmpty(vals ...string) string {
937		for _, v := range vals {
938			v = strings.TrimSpace(v)
939			if v != "" {
940				return v
941			}
942		}
943		return ""
944	}
945	
946	func parseCodexFunctionOutput(
947		payload gjson.Result,
948	) (gjson.Result, string) {
949		out := payload.Get("output")
950		if !out.Exists() {
951			return gjson.Result{}, ""
952		}
953	
954		switch out.Type {
955		case gjson.String:
956			s := strings.TrimSpace(out.Str)
957			if s == "" {
958				return gjson.Result{}, ""
959			}
960			if gjson.Valid(s) {
961				return gjson.Parse(s), s
962			}
963			return gjson.Result{}, s
964		default:
965			raw := strings.TrimSpace(out.Raw)
966			if raw == "" {
967				return gjson.Result{}, ""
968			}
969			if gjson.Valid(raw) {
970				return gjson.Parse(raw), raw
971			}
972			return gjson.Result{}, raw
973		}
974	}
975	
976	func codexWaitAgentIDs(args gjson.Result) []string {
977		if !args.Exists() {
978			return nil
979		}
980		ids := args.Get("ids")
981		if !ids.Exists() {
982			ids = args.Get("targets")
983		}
984		if !ids.Exists() || !ids.IsArray() {
985			return nil
986		}
987	
988		var out []string
989		for _, item := range ids.Array() {
990			id := strings.TrimSpace(item.Str)
991			if id == "" {
992				continue
993			}
994			out = append(out, id)
995		}
996		return out
997	}
998	
999	func isCodexWaitAgentCall(name string) bool {
1000		return name == "wait" || name == "wait_agent"
1001	}
1002	
1003	func parseCodexSubagentNotification(
1004		content string,
1005	) (agentID, statusName, text string) {
1006		if !isCodexSubagentNotification(content) {
1007			return "", "", ""
1008		}
1009		body := strings.TrimSpace(content)
1010		body = strings.TrimPrefix(body, "<subagent_notification>")
1011		body = strings.TrimSuffix(body, "</subagent_notification>")
1012		body = strings.TrimSpace(body)
1013		if !gjson.Valid(body) {
1014			return "", "", ""
1015		}
1016		parsed := gjson.Parse(body)
1017		agentID = firstNonEmpty(
1018			parsed.Get("agent_id").Str,
1019			parsed.Get("agent_path").Str,
1020		)
1021		status := parsed.Get("status")
1022		statusName, text = codexTerminalSubagentEvent(status)
1023		return agentID, statusName, text
1024	}
1025	
1026	func codexTerminalSubagentEvent(status gjson.Result) (string, string) {
1027		if text := strings.TrimSpace(status.Get("completed").Str); text != "" {
1028			return "completed", text
1029		}
1030		if text := strings.TrimSpace(status.Get("errored").Str); text != "" {
1031			return "errored", text
1032		}
1033		if text := strings.TrimSpace(status.Get("running").Str); text != "" {
1034			return "running", text
1035		}
1036		return "", ""
1037	}
1038	
1039	func codexTerminalSubagentStatus(status gjson.Result) string {
1040		_, text := codexTerminalSubagentEvent(status)
1041		return text
1042	}
1043	
1044	func isCodexSubagentFunctionOutput(output gjson.Result) bool {
1045		if !output.Exists() {
1046			return false
1047		}
1048		if strings.TrimSpace(output.Get("agent_id").Str) != "" {
1049			return true
1050		}
1051	
1052		status := output.Get("status")
1053		if !status.Exists() || !status.IsObject() {
1054			return false
1055		}
1056		entries := status.Map()
1057		if len(entries) == 0 {
1058			return false
1059		}
1060		for agentID, entry := range entries {
1061			if strings.TrimSpace(agentID) == "" || !entry.IsObject() {
1062				return false
1063			}
1064			if codexTerminalSubagentStatus(entry) != "" {
1065				continue
1066			}
1067			if strings.TrimSpace(entry.Get("running").Str) != "" {
1068				continue
1069			}
1070			return false

1273	func ParseCodexSessionFrom(

1324	func isCodexSystemMessage(content string) bool {
1325		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)
1326		return strings.HasPrefix(content, "# AGENTS.md") ||
1327			strings.HasPrefix(content, "<environment_context>") ||
1328			strings.HasPrefix(content, "<INSTRUCTIONS>") ||
1329			strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<turn_aborted>") ||
1330			strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<skill>") ||
1331			isCodexSubagentNotification(content)
1332	}

1334	func isCodexSubagentNotification(content string) bool {
1335		return strings.HasPrefix(
1336			strings.TrimSpace(content),
1337			"<subagent_notification>",
1338		)
1339	}

1341	func codexIncrementalNeedsFullParse(line string) bool {
1342		switch gjson.Get(line, "type").Str {
1343		case codexTypeEventMsg:
1344			return gjson.Get(line, "payload.type").Str ==
1345				"collab_agent_spawn_end"
1346		case codexTypeResponseItem:
1347		default:
1348			return false
1349		}
1350	
1351		payload := gjson.Get(line, "payload")
1352		switch payload.Get("type").Str {
1353		case "function_call":
1354			return isCodexWaitAgentCall(payload.Get("name").Str)
1355		case "function_call_output":
1356			output, _ := parseCodexFunctionOutput(payload)
1357			return isCodexSubagentFunctionOutput(output)
1358		default:
1359			role := payload.Get("role").Str
1360			if role != "user" {
1361				return false
1362			}
1363			agentID, _, text := parseCodexSubagentNotification(
1364				extractCodexContent(payload),
1365			)
1366			return agentID != "" && text != ""
1367		}
1368	}
