346		path string,
347		offset int64,
348		startOrdinal int,
349	) ([]ParsedMessage, time.Time, int64, error) {
350		var (
351			entries        []dagEntry
352			queuedCommands []claudeQueuedCommand
353			lineIndex      = startOrdinal
354			// Track latest timestamp from all lines, including
355			// non-message events (progress, queue-operation) so
356			// callers can update ended_at even when no new
357			// messages are found.
358			latestTS time.Time
359		)
360	
361		consumed, err := readJSONLFrom(
362			path, offset, func(line string) {
363				if ts := extractTimestamp(line); !ts.IsZero() {
364					if ts.After(latestTS) {
365						latestTS = ts
366					}
367				}
368				entryType := gjson.Get(line, "type").Str
369				if entryType == "attachment" {
370					if qc, ok := extractQueuedCommand(line); ok {
371						queuedCommands = append(queuedCommands, qc)
372					}
373					return
374				}
375				if entryType != "user" &&
376					entryType != "assistant" {
377					return
378				}
379				ts := extractTimestamp(line)
380				entries = append(entries, dagEntry{
381					uuid:       gjson.Get(line, "uuid").Str,
382					parentUuid: gjson.Get(line, "parentUuid").Str,
383					entryType:  entryType,
384					lineIndex:  lineIndex,
385					line:       line,
386					timestamp:  ts,
387				})
388				lineIndex++
389			},
390		)
391		if err != nil {
392			return nil, time.Time{}, 0, fmt.Errorf(
393				"reading claude %s from offset %d: %w",
394				path, offset, err,
395			)
396		}
397	
398		if len(entries) == 0 && len(queuedCommands) == 0 {
399			return nil, latestTS, consumed, nil
400		}
401	
402		// Detect forks: if any entry's parentUuid doesn't
403		// match the previous entry's uuid, the appended data
404		// contains a branch that requires full DAG processing.
405		if hasDAGFork(entries) {
406			return nil, time.Time{}, 0, ErrDAGDetected
407		}
408	
409		// Subagent linkage updates (toolUseResult.agentId) and
410		// same-message.id chunk merging both need state the full
411		// parser builds across the whole file. Bail to a full parse
412		// when appended lines contain either.
413		if needsClaudeFullParse(entries) {
414			return nil, time.Time{}, 0,
415				ErrClaudeIncrementalNeedsFullParse
416		}
417	
418		msgs, _, endedAt := extractMessagesFrom(
419			entries, startOrdinal,
420		)
421		if len(queuedCommands) > 0 {
422			msgs = mergeQueuedCommands(
423				msgs, queuedCommands, startOrdinal,
424			)
425			for _, qc := range queuedCommands {
426				if qc.timestamp.After(endedAt) {
427					endedAt = qc.timestamp
428				}
429			}
430		}
431		// Use the latest timestamp from all lines (including
432		// non-message events) if it's later than what
433		// extractMessagesFrom found.
434		if latestTS.After(endedAt) {
435			endedAt = latestTS
436		}
437		return msgs, endedAt, consumed, nil
438	}
439	
440	// needsClaudeFullParse returns true when appended entries contain
441	// either a tool_result with toolUseResult.agentId (whose linkage
442	// must update an already-stored tool_call row) or a consecutive
443	// same-message.id assistant run (whose chunks the full parser
444	// merges into one message). Both cases require a full re-parse.
445	func needsClaudeFullParse(entries []dagEntry) bool {
446		var prevAssistantMID string
447		for _, e := range entries {
448			if e.entryType == "user" {
449				if gjson.Get(e.line, "toolUseResult.agentId").Str != "" {
450					return true
451				}
452			}
453			if e.entryType == "assistant" {
454				mid := gjson.Get(e.line, "message.id").Str
455				if mid != "" && mid == prevAssistantMID {
456					return true
457				}
458				prevAssistantMID = mid
459				continue
460			}
461			prevAssistantMID = ""
462		}
463		return false
464	}
465	
466	// hasDAGFork returns true if the entries contain a fork —
467	// i.e. any entry whose parentUuid doesn't point to the
468	// immediately preceding entry's uuid. Linear UUID chains
469	// (each entry parenting the next) are safe for incremental
470	// parsing; forks require full DAG processing.
471	func hasDAGFork(entries []dagEntry) bool {
472		var lastUUID string
473		for _, e := range entries {
474			if e.uuid == "" {
475				continue // non-UUID entries are always linear
476			}
477			if lastUUID != "" &&
478				e.parentUuid != lastUUID {
479				return true
480			}
481			lastUUID = e.uuid
482		}
483		return false
484	}
485	
486	// extractMessagesFrom is like extractMessages but uses a
487	// custom starting ordinal for incremental parsing.
488	func extractMessagesFrom(
489		entries []dagEntry, startOrdinal int,
490	) ([]ParsedMessage, time.Time, time.Time) {
491		var (
492			messages  []ParsedMessage
493			startedAt time.Time
494			endedAt   time.Time
495			ordinal   = startOrdinal
496		)
497	
498		for _, e := range entries {
499			if !e.timestamp.IsZero() {
500				if startedAt.IsZero() {
501					startedAt = e.timestamp
502				}
503				endedAt = e.timestamp
504			}
505	
506			// Detect compact summaries before the user/assistant
507			// gates: Claude can emit isCompactSummary=true with
508			// either top-level type, and the record must always
509			// be persisted as a system boundary regardless.
510			if gjson.Get(e.line, "isCompactSummary").Bool() {
511				summary := extractCompactSummary(e.line)
512				messages = append(messages, ParsedMessage{
513					Ordinal:           ordinal,
514					Role:              RoleAssistant,
515					Content:           summary,
516					Timestamp:         e.timestamp,
517					IsSystem:          true,
518					ContentLength:     len(summary),
519					SourceType:        "system",
520					SourceSubtype:     "compact_boundary",
521					SourceUUID:        e.uuid,
522					SourceParentUUID:  e.parentUuid,
523					IsSidechain:       gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
524					IsCompactBoundary: true,
525				})
526				ordinal++
527				continue
528			}
529	
530			if e.entryType == "user" {
531				if gjson.Get(e.line, "isMeta").Bool() {
532					continue
533				}
534			}
535	
536			content := gjson.Get(e.line, "message.content")
537			text, thinkingText, hasThinking, hasToolUse, tcs, trs :=
538				ExtractTextContent(content)
539	
540			// Convert command/skill invocation XML into readable
541			// text (e.g. "/roborev-fix 450"). If the content
542			// looks like a command envelope but can't be
543			// normalized, skip it to avoid raw XML in transcripts.
544			if e.entryType == "user" {
545				if cmdText, ok := extractCommandText(text); ok {
546					text = cmdText
547				} else if isCommandEnvelope(text) {
548					continue
549				}
550			}
551	
552			if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" && len(trs) == 0 {
553				continue
554			}
555	
556			if e.entryType == "user" {
557				if subtype := ClassifyClaudeSystemMessage(text); subtype != "" {
558					// Preserve Role=user so analytics that compute
559					// turn-cycle/throughput on role alone (see
560					// internal/db/analytics.go) don't count these as
561					// assistant replies. is_system + source_subtype
562					// let the UI and filters route them correctly.
563					messages = append(messages, ParsedMessage{
564						Ordinal:          ordinal,
565						Role:             RoleUser,
566						Content:          text,
567						Timestamp:        e.timestamp,
568						IsSystem:         true,
569						ContentLength:    len(text),
570						SourceType:       "system",
571						SourceSubtype:    subtype,
572						SourceUUID:       e.uuid,
573						SourceParentUUID: e.parentUuid,
574						IsSidechain:      gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
575					})
576					ordinal++
577					continue
578				}
579				// Skip unclassified noise (e.g. non-caveat
580				// <local-command-*> envelopes).
581				if isClaudeSystemMessage(text) {
582					continue
583				}
584			}
585	
586			msg := ParsedMessage{
587				Ordinal:            ordinal,
588				Role:               RoleType(e.entryType),
589				Content:            text,
590				ThinkingText:       thinkingText,
591				Timestamp:          e.timestamp,
592				HasThinking:        hasThinking,
593				HasToolUse:         hasToolUse,
594				ContentLength:      len(text),
595				ToolCalls:          tcs,
596				ToolResults:        trs,
597				SourceType:         e.entryType,
598				SourceUUID:         e.uuid,
599				SourceParentUUID:   e.parentUuid,
600				IsSidechain:        gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
601				tokenPresenceKnown: e.entryType == "assistant",
602			}
603	
604			if e.entryType == "assistant" {
605				extractClaudeTokenFields(&msg, e.line)
606				msg.StopReason = gjson.Get(e.line, "message.stop_reason").Str
607			}
608	
609			messages = append(messages, msg)
610			ordinal++
611		}
612	
613		return messages, startedAt, endedAt
614	}
615	
616	// claudeSessionMeta holds source metadata extracted during the
617	// main parse loop and applied to all resulting ParsedSessions.
618	type claudeSessionMeta struct {
619		sourceSessionID string
620		sourceVersion   string
621		cwd             string
622		gitBranch       string
623		malformedLines  int
624		isTruncated     bool
625	}
626	
627	// applyTo sets source metadata fields on a ParsedSession.
628	func (m claudeSessionMeta) applyTo(sess *ParsedSession) {
629		sess.SourceSessionID = m.sourceSessionID
630		sess.SourceVersion = m.sourceVersion
631		sess.Cwd = m.cwd
632		sess.GitBranch = m.gitBranch
633		sess.MalformedLines = m.malformedLines
634		sess.IsTruncated = m.isTruncated
635	}
636	
637	// parseLinear processes entries sequentially without DAG awareness.
638	func parseLinear(
639		entries []dagEntry,
640		sessionID, project, machine, parentSessionID string,
641		fileInfo FileInfo,
642		subagentMap map[string]string,
643		globalStart, globalEnd time.Time,
644		meta claudeSessionMeta,
645	) ([]ParseResult, error) {
646		messages, startedAt, endedAt := extractMessages(entries)
647		startedAt = earlierTime(globalStart, startedAt)
648		endedAt = laterTime(globalEnd, endedAt)
649		annotateSubagentSessions(messages, subagentMap)
650	
651		// Promoted system messages (continuation/resume/interrupted/
652		// task_notification/stop_hook) carry Role=user so role-keyed
653		// analytics ignore them, but they are not real user turns;
654		// firstMessageAndUserCount skips them when computing
655		// user_message_count / first_message. It also skips leading
656		// /clear and /effort command envelopes so the sidebar shows
657		// the next real message instead of the command.
658		firstMsg, userCount := firstMessageAndUserCount(messages)
659	
660		sess := ParsedSession{
661			ID:               sessionID,
662			Project:          project,
663			Machine:          machine,
664			Agent:            AgentClaude,
665			ParentSessionID:  parentSessionID,
666			FirstMessage:     firstMsg,
667			StartedAt:        startedAt,
668			EndedAt:          endedAt,
669			MessageCount:     len(messages),
670			UserMessageCount: userCount,
671			File:             fileInfo,
672		}
673		meta.applyTo(&sess)
674		accumulateMessageTokenUsage(&sess, messages)
675	
676		return []ParseResult{{Session: sess, Messages: messages}}, nil
677	}
678	
679	// parseDAG builds a parent->children adjacency map and walks the
680	// tree to detect fork points. Large-gap forks produce separate
681	// ParseResults; small-gap retries follow the latest branch.
682	func parseDAG(
683		entries []dagEntry,
684		sessionID, project, machine, parentSessionID string,
685		fileInfo FileInfo,
686		subagentMap map[string]string,
687		globalStart, globalEnd time.Time,
688		meta claudeSessionMeta,
689	) ([]ParseResult, error) {
690		// Build parent -> children ordered by line position and
691		// collect the set of all uuids for connectivity checks.
692		children := make(map[string][]int, len(entries))
693		uuidSet := make(map[string]struct{}, len(entries))
694		var roots []int
695		for i, e := range entries {
696			if e.uuid != "" {
697				uuidSet[e.uuid] = struct{}{}
698			}
699			if e.parentUuid == "" {
700				roots = append(roots, i)
701			} else {
702				children[e.parentUuid] = append(children[e.parentUuid], i)
703			}
704		}
705	
706		// A well-formed DAG has exactly one root and all parentUuid
707		// references resolve to an existing entry's uuid. If not,
708		// fall back to linear parsing to avoid dropping messages.
709		if len(roots) != 1 {
710			return parseLinear(
711				entries, sessionID, project, machine,
712				parentSessionID, fileInfo, subagentMap,
713				globalStart, globalEnd, meta,
714			)
715		}
716		for _, e := range entries {
717			if e.parentUuid != "" {
718				if _, ok := uuidSet[e.parentUuid]; !ok {
719					return parseLinear(
720						entries, sessionID, project, machine,
721						parentSessionID, fileInfo, subagentMap,
722						globalStart, globalEnd, meta,
723					)
724				}
725			}
726		}
727	
728		// Walk from the root, collecting branches.
729		// branches[0] is the main branch; subsequent entries are forks.
730		type branch struct {
731			indices  []int
732			parentID string // immediate parent session ID
733		}
734	
735		var branches []branch
736	
737		// walkBranch follows the DAG from a starting index, collecting
738		// all entries on the chosen path. At fork points, it either
739		// follows the latest child (small gap) or splits (large gap).
740		// ownerID is the session ID of the branch that owns this walk.
741		var walkBranch func(startIdx int, ownerID string) []int
742		var forkBranches []branch
743	
744		walkBranch = func(startIdx int, ownerID string) []int {
745			var path []int
746			current := startIdx
747	
748			for current >= 0 {
749				path = append(path, current)
750				uuid := entries[current].uuid
751				kids := children[uuid]
752				if len(kids) == 0 {
753					break
754				}
755				if len(kids) == 1 {
756					current = kids[0]
757					continue
758				}
759	
760				// Fork point: count user turns on first child's branch.
761				firstChildTurns := countUserTurns(entries, children, kids[0])
762				if firstChildTurns <= forkThreshold {
763					// Small-gap retry: follow the last child.
764					current = kids[len(kids)-1]
765				} else {
766					// Large-gap fork: follow first child on main,
767					// collect other children as fork branches.
768					for _, kid := range kids[1:] {
769						forkSID := sessionID + "-" +
770							entries[kid].uuid
771						forkPath := walkBranch(kid, forkSID)
772						forkBranches = append(
773							forkBranches,
774							branch{
775								indices:  forkPath,
776								parentID: ownerID,
777							},
778						)
779					}
780					current = kids[0]
781				}
782			}
783	
784			return path
785		}
786	
787		mainPath := walkBranch(roots[0], sessionID)
788		branches = append(
789			branches,
790			branch{indices: mainPath, parentID: parentSessionID},
791		)
792		branches = append(branches, forkBranches...)
793	
794		// Build results for each branch.
795		var results []ParseResult
796	
797		for i, b := range branches {
798			branchEntries := make([]dagEntry, len(b.indices))
799			for j, idx := range b.indices {
800				branchEntries[j] = entries[idx]
801			}
802	
803			messages, startedAt, endedAt := extractMessages(branchEntries)
804			// Main session uses global bounds to capture timestamps
805			// from non-message events (e.g. queue-operation).
806			if i == 0 {
807				startedAt = earlierTime(globalStart, startedAt)
808				endedAt = laterTime(globalEnd, endedAt)
809			}
810			annotateSubagentSessions(messages, subagentMap)
811	
812			firstMsg, userCount := firstMessageAndUserCount(messages)
813	
814			sid := sessionID
815			pSID := b.parentID
816			relType := RelationshipType("")
817	
818			if i > 0 {
819				// Fork session: ID derived from first entry's uuid,
820				// parent is the branch that forked.
821				firstEntry := entries[b.indices[0]]
822				sid = sessionID + "-" + firstEntry.uuid
823				relType = RelFork
824			}
825	
826			sess := ParsedSession{
827				ID:               sid,
828				Project:          project,
829				Machine:          machine,
830				Agent:            AgentClaude,
831				ParentSessionID:  pSID,
832				RelationshipType: relType,
833				FirstMessage:     firstMsg,
834				StartedAt:        startedAt,
835				EndedAt:          endedAt,
836				MessageCount:     len(messages),
837				UserMessageCount: userCount,
838				File:             fileInfo,
839			}
840			meta.applyTo(&sess)
841			accumulateMessageTokenUsage(&sess, messages)
842	
843			results = append(results, ParseResult{
844				Session:  sess,
845				Messages: messages,
846			})
847		}
848	
849		return results, nil
850	}
851	
852	func collectToolResultAgentID(line string, subagentMap map[string]string) {
853		agentID := gjson.Get(line, "toolUseResult.agentId").Str
854		if agentID == "" {
855			return
856		}
857		sessionID := agentID
858		if !strings.HasPrefix(sessionID, "agent-") {
859			sessionID = "agent-" + sessionID
860		}
861	
862		content := gjson.Get(line, "message.content")
863		if !content.IsArray() {
864			return
865		}
866		var toolUseID string
867		content.ForEach(func(_, block gjson.Result) bool {
868			if block.Get("type").Str != "tool_result" {
869				return true
870			}
871			tuid := block.Get("tool_use_id").Str
872			if tuid == "" {
873				return true
874			}
875			if toolUseID != "" {
876				toolUseID = ""
877				return false
878			}
879			toolUseID = tuid
880			return true
881		})
882		if toolUseID == "" {
883			return
884		}
885		if _, exists := subagentMap[toolUseID]; !exists {
886			subagentMap[toolUseID] = sessionID
887		}
888	}
889	
890	// extractQueuedCommand parses a Claude Code attachment entry and
891	// returns the queued_command prompt if present. Other attachment
892	// types (e.g. task_reminder) return ok=false. Whitespace-only or
893	// empty prompts also return false to match the parser's general
894	// "skip empty user content" behavior.
895	func extractQueuedCommand(line string) (claudeQueuedCommand, bool) {
896		if gjson.Get(line, "attachment.type").Str != "queued_command" {
897			return claudeQueuedCommand{}, false
898		}
899		prompt := gjson.Get(line, "attachment.prompt").Str
900		if strings.TrimSpace(prompt) == "" {
901			return claudeQueuedCommand{}, false
902		}
903		return claudeQueuedCommand{
904			prompt:    prompt,
905			timestamp: extractTimestamp(line),
906		}, true
907	}
908	
909	// applyQueuedCommands splices queued_command attachments into a
910	// ParseResult by timestamp, renumbers ordinals, and refreshes
911	// derived session counts. Token aggregates are unchanged because
912	// queued_command entries have no usage data. Callers must ensure
913	// queued is non-empty.
914	func applyQueuedCommands(
915		r ParseResult, queued []claudeQueuedCommand,
916	) ParseResult {
917		merged := mergeQueuedCommands(r.Messages, queued, 0)
918		firstMsg, userCount := firstMessageAndUserCount(merged)
919		r.Session.FirstMessage = firstMsg
920		r.Session.UserMessageCount = userCount
921		r.Session.MessageCount = len(merged)
922		for _, qc := range queued {
923			if qc.timestamp.After(r.Session.EndedAt) {
924				r.Session.EndedAt = qc.timestamp
925			}
926			if !qc.timestamp.IsZero() &&
927				(r.Session.StartedAt.IsZero() ||
928					qc.timestamp.Before(r.Session.StartedAt)) {
929				r.Session.StartedAt = qc.timestamp
930			}
931		}
932		r.Messages = merged
933		return r
934	}
935	
936	// mergeQueuedCommands merges queued_command entries into messages
937	// in timestamp order and renumbers ordinals starting at the given
938	// offset. Both inputs are assumed to already be in chronological
939	// order. Equal timestamps preserve the original message before the
940	// queued command (queued commands always follow the entry that
941	// triggered the tool call).
942	func mergeQueuedCommands(
943		messages []ParsedMessage,
944		queued []claudeQueuedCommand,
945		startOrdinal int,
946	) []ParsedMessage {
947		out := make([]ParsedMessage, 0, len(messages)+len(queued))
948		i, j := 0, 0
949		for i < len(messages) && j < len(queued) {
950			if queuedBefore(queued[j], messages[i]) {
951				out = append(out, queuedCommandMessage(queued[j]))
952				j++
953			} else {
954				out = append(out, messages[i])
955				i++
956			}
957		}
958		for ; i < len(messages); i++ {
959			out = append(out, messages[i])
960		}
961		for ; j < len(queued); j++ {
962			out = append(out, queuedCommandMessage(queued[j]))
963		}
964		for k := range out {
965			out[k].Ordinal = startOrdinal + k
966		}
967		return out
968	}
969	
970	// queuedBefore reports whether a queued_command should sort before
971	// a regular message. Zero timestamps on either side are treated
972	// conservatively: a zero-timestamp message keeps its original
973	// position relative to queued items.
974	func queuedBefore(
975		q claudeQueuedCommand, m ParsedMessage,
976	) bool {
977		if q.timestamp.IsZero() {
978			return false
979		}
980		if m.Timestamp.IsZero() {
981			return false
982		}
983		return q.timestamp.Before(m.Timestamp)
984	}
985	
986	// queuedCommandMessage builds a ParsedMessage from a collected
987	// queued_command attachment. Role stays user (the user typed
988	// this) and IsSystem is false so it counts as a real user turn;
989	// SourceSubtype lets the UI distinguish it from inline prompts.
990	func queuedCommandMessage(
991		q claudeQueuedCommand,
992	) ParsedMessage {
993		return ParsedMessage{
994			Role:          RoleUser,
995			Content:       q.prompt,
996			Timestamp:     q.timestamp,
997			ContentLength: len(q.prompt),
998			SourceType:    "user",
999			SourceSubtype: "queued_command",
1000		}
1001	}
1002	
1003	// mergeClaudeAssistantMessageChunks merges consecutive assistant
1004	// entries that share the same message.id. Claude Code uses this shape
1005	// both for cumulative streaming snapshots and for additive chunks of a
1006	// single response. The last entry owns metadata and token usage; the
1007	// merged message content keeps each distinct block in first-seen order.
1008	func mergeClaudeAssistantMessageChunks(entries []dagEntry) []dagEntry {
1009		if len(entries) <= 1 {
1010			return entries
1011		}
1012	
1013		result := make([]dagEntry, 0, len(entries))
1014		for i := 0; i < len(entries); i++ {
1015			mid := ""
1016			if entries[i].entryType == "assistant" {
1017				mid = gjson.Get(entries[i].line, "message.id").Str
1018			}
1019			if mid == "" {
1020				result = append(result, entries[i])
1021				continue
1022			}
1023	
1024			j := i + 1
1025			for j < len(entries) &&
1026				entries[j].entryType == "assistant" &&
1027				gjson.Get(entries[j].line, "message.id").Str == mid {
1028				j++
1029			}
1030			if j == i+1 {
1031				result = append(result, entries[i])
1032			} else {
1033				result = append(result, mergeClaudeAssistantRun(entries[i:j]))
1034			}
1035			i = j - 1
1036		}
1037		return result
1038	}
1039	
1040	// mergeClaudeAssistantRun collapses one same-message.id assistant
1041	// run into a single dagEntry. For each snapshot in the run we decide
1042	// whether it is a cumulative continuation of the merged-so-far (its
1043	// leading blocks align by type, tool_use id, and text equal-or-prefix)
1044	// or an additive chunk (distinct new content). Cumulative snapshots
1045	// update overlapping positions in place and append any trailing blocks;
1046	// additive snapshots append blocks not already present.
1047	//
1048	// Once any entry in the run has stop_reason="end_turn", the message
1049	// has terminated; subsequent same-message.id entries are treated as
1050	// additive distinct chunks rather than streaming snapshots, even if
1051	// their text would otherwise prefix-match.
1052	func mergeClaudeAssistantRun(run []dagEntry) dagEntry {
1053		base := run[len(run)-1]
1054		var merged []gjson.Result
1055		// Once a snapshot in the run has stop_reason="end_turn" the
1056		// message has terminated. Any further same-message.id entries
1057		// are additive distinct chunks rather than streaming snapshots,
1058		// so cumulative prefix-matching must be skipped.
1059		runEnded := false
1060	
1061		for _, e := range run {
1062			content := gjson.Get(e.line, "message.content")
1063			if !content.IsArray() {
1064				continue
1065			}
1066			merged = mergeClaudeSnapshot(
1067				merged, claudeContentBlocks(content), runEnded,
1068			)
1069			if gjson.Get(e.line, "message.stop_reason").Str == "end_turn" {
1070				runEnded = true
1071			}
1072		}
1073		if len(merged) == 0 {
1074			return base
1075		}
1076		base.line = replaceClaudeMessageContent(base.line, merged)
1077		return base
1078	}
1079	
1080	func claudeContentBlocks(content gjson.Result) []gjson.Result {
1081		var blocks []gjson.Result
1082		content.ForEach(func(_, b gjson.Result) bool {
1083			if b.Raw != "" {
1084				blocks = append(blocks, b)
1085			}
1086			return true
1087		})
1088		return blocks
1089	}
1090	
1091	func mergeClaudeSnapshot(
1092		merged, snapshot []gjson.Result, runEnded bool,
1093	) []gjson.Result {
1094		if !runEnded && claudeSnapshotIsCumulative(merged, snapshot) {
1095			for i, block := range snapshot {
1096				if i < len(merged) {
1097					merged[i] = pickClaudeLatestBlock(merged[i], block)
1098					continue
1099				}
1100				merged = append(merged, block)
1101			}
1102			return merged
1103		}
1104		for _, block := range snapshot {
1105			if !claudeBlockExistsIn(block, merged) {
1106				merged = append(merged, block)
1107			}
1108		}
1109		return merged
1110	}
1111	
1112	func claudeSnapshotIsCumulative(
1113		merged, snapshot []gjson.Result,
1114	) bool {
1115		if len(merged) == 0 || len(snapshot) == 0 {
1116			return true
1117		}
1118		n := min(len(snapshot), len(merged))
1119		for i := range n {
1120			if !claudeBlocksAlign(merged[i], snapshot[i]) {
1121				return false
1122			}
1123		}
1124		return true
1125	}
1126	
1127	func claudeBlocksAlign(a, b gjson.Result) bool {
1128		if a.Get("type").Str != b.Get("type").Str {
1129			return false
1130		}
1131		switch a.Get("type").Str {
1132		case "text":
1133			ta := a.Get("text").Str
1134			tb := b.Get("text").Str
1135			return ta == tb ||
1136				strings.HasPrefix(tb, ta) ||
1137				strings.HasPrefix(ta, tb)
1138		case "tool_use":
1139			ida := a.Get("id").Str
1140			idb := b.Get("id").Str
1141			if ida != "" && idb != "" {
1142				return ida == idb
1143			}
1144			return a.Raw == b.Raw
1145		default:
1146			return a.Raw == b.Raw
1147		}
1148	}
1149	
1150	func pickClaudeLatestBlock(existing, candidate gjson.Result) gjson.Result {
1151		if existing.Get("type").Str != candidate.Get("type").Str {
1152			return candidate
1153		}
1154		switch existing.Get("type").Str {
1155		case "text":
1156			if len(candidate.Get("text").Str) >=
1157				len(existing.Get("text").Str) {
1158				return candidate
1159			}
1160			return existing
1161		case "tool_use":
1162			return candidate
1163		default:
1164			return existing
1165		}
1166	}
1167	
1168	func claudeBlockExistsIn(
1169		target gjson.Result, blocks []gjson.Result,
1170	) bool {
1171		targetType := target.Get("type").Str
1172		targetID := target.Get("id").Str
1173		for _, b := range blocks {
1174			if b.Get("type").Str != targetType {
1175				continue
1176			}
1177			if targetType == "tool_use" && targetID != "" {
1178				if b.Get("id").Str == targetID {
1179					return true
1180				}
1181				continue
1182			}
1183			if b.Raw == target.Raw {
1184				return true
1185			}
1186		}
1187		return false
1188	}
1189	
1190	func replaceClaudeMessageContent(line string, blocks []gjson.Result) string {
1191		// UseNumber preserves the raw textual form of JSON numbers so
1192		// re-marshaling doesn't truncate large integers (e.g. usage
1193		// token counts) or change scientific notation.
1194		dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(line))
1195		dec.UseNumber()
1196		var top map[string]any
1197		if err := dec.Decode(&top); err != nil {
1198			return line
1199		}
1200		msg, ok := top["message"].(map[string]any)
1201		if !ok {
1202			return line
1203		}
1204		content := make([]json.RawMessage, 0, len(blocks))
1205		for _, block := range blocks {
1206			if block.Raw == "" {
1207				continue
1208			}
1209			content = append(content, json.RawMessage(block.Raw))
1210		}
1211		msg["content"] = content
1212		encoded, err := json.Marshal(top)
1213		if err != nil {
1214			return line
1215		}
1216		return string(encoded)
1217	}
1218	
1219	// countUserTurns counts all user entries reachable from a
1220	// starting index by traversing the entire subtree. Earlier
1221	// versions followed only the first child at each node, which
1222	// undercounted in sessions with many nested forks and caused
1223	// the fork heuristic to discard the main conversation branch.
1224	func countUserTurns(
1225		entries []dagEntry,
1226		children map[string][]int,
1227		startIdx int,
1228	) int {
1229		count := 0
1230		stack := []int{startIdx}
1231		for len(stack) > 0 {
1232			current := stack[len(stack)-1]
1233			stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
1234			if entries[current].entryType == "user" {
1235				count++
1236			}
1237			stack = append(stack, children[entries[current].uuid]...)
1238		}
1239		return count
1240	}
1241	
1242	// extractMessages converts dagEntries into ParsedMessages, applying
1243	// the same filtering and content extraction as the original linear
1244	// parser.
1245	func extractMessages(entries []dagEntry) (
1246		[]ParsedMessage, time.Time, time.Time,
1247	) {
1248		var (
1249			messages  []ParsedMessage
1250			startedAt time.Time
1251			endedAt   time.Time
1252			ordinal   int
1253		)
1254	
1255		for _, e := range entries {
1256			if !e.timestamp.IsZero() {
1257				if startedAt.IsZero() {
1258					startedAt = e.timestamp
1259				}
1260				endedAt = e.timestamp
1261			}
1262	
1263			// Detect compact summaries before the user/assistant
1264			// gates: Claude can emit isCompactSummary=true with
1265			// either top-level type, and the record must always
1266			// be persisted as a system boundary regardless.
1267			if gjson.Get(e.line, "isCompactSummary").Bool() {
1268				summary := extractCompactSummary(e.line)
1269				messages = append(messages, ParsedMessage{
1270					Ordinal:           ordinal,
1271					Role:              RoleAssistant,
1272					Content:           summary,
1273					Timestamp:         e.timestamp,
1274					IsSystem:          true,
1275					ContentLength:     len(summary),
1276					SourceType:        "system",
1277					SourceSubtype:     "compact_boundary",
1278					SourceUUID:        e.uuid,
1279					SourceParentUUID:  e.parentUuid,
1280					IsSidechain:       gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
1281					IsCompactBoundary: true,
1282				})
1283				ordinal++
1284				continue
1285			}
1286	
1287			// Tier 1: skip system-injected user entries.
1288			if e.entryType == "user" {
1289				if gjson.Get(e.line, "isMeta").Bool() {
1290					continue
1291				}
1292			}
1293	
1294			content := gjson.Get(e.line, "message.content")
1295			text, thinkingText, hasThinking, hasToolUse, tcs, trs :=
1296				ExtractTextContent(content)
1297	
1298			// Convert command/skill invocation XML into readable
1299			// text (e.g. "/roborev-fix 450"). If the content
1300			// looks like a command envelope but can't be
1301			// normalized, skip it to avoid raw XML in transcripts.
1302			if e.entryType == "user" {
1303				if cmdText, ok := extractCommandText(text); ok {
1304					text = cmdText
1305				} else if isCommandEnvelope(text) {
1306					continue
1307				}
1308			}
1309	
1310			if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" && len(trs) == 0 {
1311				continue
1312			}
1313	
1314			// Tier 2: promote classifiable system-injected patterns
1315			// to source_subtype messages; skip unclassified noise
1316			// (e.g. non-caveat <local-command-*> envelopes). Role
1317			// stays "user" so role-keyed analytics continue to treat
1318			// these as inputs, not assistant replies.
1319			if e.entryType == "user" {
1320				if subtype := ClassifyClaudeSystemMessage(text); subtype != "" {
1321					messages = append(messages, ParsedMessage{
1322						Ordinal:          ordinal,
1323						Role:             RoleUser,
1324						Content:          text,
1325						Timestamp:        e.timestamp,
1326						IsSystem:         true,
1327						ContentLength:    len(text),
1328						SourceType:       "system",
1329						SourceSubtype:    subtype,
1330						SourceUUID:       e.uuid,
1331						SourceParentUUID: e.parentUuid,
1332						IsSidechain:      gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
1333					})
1334					ordinal++
1335					continue
1336				}
1337				if isClaudeSystemMessage(text) {
1338					continue
1339				}
1340			}
1341	
1342			msg := ParsedMessage{
1343				Ordinal:            ordinal,
1344				Role:               RoleType(e.entryType),
1345				Content:            text,
1346				ThinkingText:       thinkingText,
1347				Timestamp:          e.timestamp,
1348				HasThinking:        hasThinking,
1349				HasToolUse:         hasToolUse,
1350				ContentLength:      len(text),
1351				ToolCalls:          tcs,
1352				ToolResults:        trs,
1353				SourceType:         e.entryType,
1354				SourceUUID:         e.uuid,
1355				SourceParentUUID:   e.parentUuid,
1356				IsSidechain:        gjson.Get(e.line, "isSidechain").Bool(),
1357				tokenPresenceKnown: e.entryType == "assistant",
1358			}
1359	
1360			if e.entryType == "assistant" {
1361				extractClaudeTokenFields(&msg, e.line)
1362				msg.StopReason = gjson.Get(e.line, "message.stop_reason").Str
1363			}
1364	
1365			messages = append(messages, msg)
1366			ordinal++
1367		}
1368	
1369		return messages, startedAt, endedAt
1370	}
1371	
1372	// extractClaudeTokenFields populates Model, TokenUsage,
1373	// ContextTokens, OutputTokens, ClaudeMessageID, and
1374	// ClaudeRequestID on a ParsedMessage from a Claude JSONL line.
1375	// Used by both full and incremental parsing paths.
1376	func extractClaudeTokenFields(msg *ParsedMessage, line string) {
1377		msg.Model = gjson.Get(line, "message.model").String()
1378		msg.ClaudeMessageID = gjson.Get(line, "message.id").String()
1379		msg.ClaudeRequestID = gjson.Get(line, "requestId").String()
1380	
1381		usageResult := gjson.Get(line, "message.usage")
1382		if usageResult.Exists() {
1383			msg.TokenUsage = json.RawMessage(usageResult.Raw)
1384			msg.HasOutputTokens = usageResult.Get("output_tokens").Exists()
1385			msg.HasContextTokens = usageResult.Get("input_tokens").Exists() ||
1386				usageResult.Get("cache_creation_input_tokens").Exists() ||
1387				usageResult.Get("cache_read_input_tokens").Exists()
1388	
1389			input := int(usageResult.Get("input_tokens").Int())
1390			cacheCreation := int(usageResult.Get(
1391				"cache_creation_input_tokens",
1392			).Int())
1393			cacheRead := int(usageResult.Get(
1394				"cache_read_input_tokens",
1395			).Int())
1396			msg.OutputTokens = int(usageResult.Get(
1397				"output_tokens",
1398			).Int())
1399			msg.ContextTokens = input + cacheCreation + cacheRead
1400		}
1401	}
1402	
1403	// annotateSubagentSessions sets SubagentSessionID on tool calls
1404	// whose ToolUseID appears in the subagentMap. Only tool calls that
1405	// represent subagent invocations (category "Task" or name containing
1406	// "subagent") are annotated.
1407	func annotateSubagentSessions(
1408		messages []ParsedMessage, subagentMap map[string]string,
1409	) {
1410		if len(subagentMap) == 0 {
1411			return
1412		}
1413		for i := range messages {
1414			for j := range messages[i].ToolCalls {
1415				tc := &messages[i].ToolCalls[j]
1416				if tc.ToolUseID == "" {
1417					continue
1418				}
1419				if sid, ok := subagentMap[tc.ToolUseID]; ok {
1420					if tc.Category == "Task" ||
1421						strings.Contains(tc.ToolName, "subagent") {
1422						tc.SubagentSessionID = sid
1423					}
1424				}
1425			}
1426		}
1427	}
1428	
1429	// extractTimestamp parses the timestamp from a JSONL line,
1430	// checking both top-level and snapshot timestamps.
1431	func extractTimestamp(line string) time.Time {
1432		tsStr := gjson.Get(line, "timestamp").Str
1433		ts := parseTimestamp(tsStr)
1434		if ts.IsZero() {
1435			snapTsStr := gjson.Get(line, "snapshot.timestamp").Str
1436			ts = parseTimestamp(snapTsStr)
1437			if ts.IsZero() {
1438				if tsStr != "" {
1439					logParseError(tsStr)
1440				} else if snapTsStr != "" {
1441					logParseError(snapTsStr)
1442				}
1443			}
1444		}
1445		return ts
1446	}
1447	
1448	// earlierTime returns the earlier of two times, ignoring zero values.
1449	func earlierTime(a, b time.Time) time.Time {
1450		if a.IsZero() {
1451			return b
1452		}
1453		if b.IsZero() {
1454			return a
1455		}
1456		if a.Before(b) {
1457			return a
1458		}
1459		return b
1460	}
1461	
1462	// laterTime returns the later of two times, ignoring zero values.
1463	func laterTime(a, b time.Time) time.Time {
1464		if a.IsZero() {
1465			return b
1466		}
1467		if b.IsZero() {
1468			return a
1469		}
1470		if a.After(b) {
1471			return a
1472		}
1473		return b
1474	}
1475	
1476	// ExtractClaudeProjectHints reads project-identifying metadata
1477	// from a Claude Code JSONL session file.
1478	func ExtractClaudeProjectHints(
1479		path string,
1480	) (cwd, gitBranch string) {
1481		f, err := os.Open(path)
1482		if err != nil {
1483			return "", ""
1484		}
1485		defer f.Close()
1486	
1487		lr := newLineReader(f, maxLineSize)
1488	
1489		for {
1490			line, ok := lr.next()
1491			if !ok {
1492				break
1493			}
1494			if !gjson.Valid(line) {
1495				continue
1496			}
1497			if gjson.Get(line, "type").Str == "user" {
1498				if cwd == "" {
1499					cwd = gjson.Get(line, "cwd").Str
1500				}
1501				if gitBranch == "" {
1502					gitBranch = gjson.Get(line, "gitBranch").Str
1503				}
1504				if cwd != "" && gitBranch != "" {
1505					return cwd, gitBranch
1506				}
1507			}
1508		}
1509		if err := lr.Err(); err != nil {
1510			log.Printf("reading hints from %s: %v", path, err)
1511		}
1512		return cwd, gitBranch
1513	}
1514	
1515	// ExtractCwdFromSession reads the first cwd field from a Claude
1516	// Code JSONL session file.
1517	func ExtractCwdFromSession(path string) string {
1518		cwd, _ := ExtractClaudeProjectHints(path)
1519		return cwd
1520	}
1521	
1522	func truncate(s string, maxLen int) string {
1523		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
1524		if len(s) <= maxLen {
1525			return s
1526		}
1527		// Truncate at a valid rune boundary to avoid producing
1528		// invalid UTF-8.
1529		r := []rune(s)
1530		if len(r) <= maxLen {
1531			return s
1532		}
1533		return string(r[:maxLen]) + "..."
1534	}
1535	
1536	// extractCommandText detects Claude Code command/skill invocation
1537	// messages and returns a human-readable representation like
1538	// "/skill-name args". Only matches messages whose trimmed content
1539	// starts with <command-message> or <command-name> (the standard
1540	// envelope format), so user messages that merely mention these
1541	// tags in prose are not affected.
1542	// Returns ("", false) if the content is not a command message.
1543	func extractCommandText(content string) (string, bool) {
1544		trimmed := strings.TrimLeftFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
1545			return r == '\uFEFF' || unicode.IsSpace(r)
1546		})
1547		if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<command-message>") &&
1548			!strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<command-name>") {
1549			return "", false
1550		}
1551		// Verify the content is purely command XML tags with no
1552		// trailing prose — strip all known tags and check the
1553		// remainder is whitespace-only.
1554		stripped := xmlCmdStripRe.ReplaceAllString(trimmed, "")
1555		if strings.TrimSpace(stripped) != "" {
1556			return "", false
1557		}
1558		m := xmlCmdNameRe.FindStringSubmatch(content)
1559		if m == nil {
1560			// Bare <command-message> without <command-name>: extract
1561			// the command-message value as a fallback.
1562			if cm := xmlCmdMsgRe.FindStringSubmatch(content); cm != nil {
1563				return "/" + cm[1], true
1564			}
1565			return "", false
1566		}
1567		name := m[1]
1568		// Ensure the name starts with "/" for display.
1569		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, "/") {
1570			name = "/" + name
1571		}
1572		args := ""
1573		if am := xmlCmdArgsRe.FindStringSubmatch(content); am != nil {
1574			args = strings.TrimSpace(am[1])
1575		}
1576		if args != "" {
1577			return name + " " + args, true
1578		}
1579		return name, true
1580	}
1581	
1582	// isCommandEnvelope returns true if the content is a pure
1583	// command XML envelope (starts with a command tag and contains
1584	// nothing but command tags and whitespace). Used as a fallback
1585	// to skip messages that look like command envelopes but couldn't
1586	// be normalized by extractCommandText.
1587	func isCommandEnvelope(content string) bool {
1588		trimmed := strings.TrimLeftFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
1589			return r == '\uFEFF' || unicode.IsSpace(r)
1590		})
1591		if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<command-message>") &&
1592			!strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<command-name>") {
1593			return false
1594		}
1595		stripped := xmlCmdStripRe.ReplaceAllString(trimmed, "")
1596		return strings.TrimSpace(stripped) == ""
1597	}
1598	
1599	// previewSkippedCommands lists Claude Code commands that should
1600	// not be used as a session's first_message preview. When a
1601	// session opens with one of these, the parser skips past it and
1602	// picks the next real user message so the sidebar shows
1603	// something descriptive.
1604	var previewSkippedCommands = []string{"/clear", "/effort"}
1605	
1606	// isSkippablePreviewCommand returns true when content is a known
1607	// Claude Code command (optionally followed by arguments), for the
1608	// purpose of skipping it when computing first_message. Match is
1609	// word-boundary: the trimmed content must equal the command
1610	// exactly or be followed by a whitespace rune, so "/clearcache"
1611	// does not match "/clear".
1612	func isSkippablePreviewCommand(content string) bool {
1613		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)
1614		for _, cmd := range previewSkippedCommands {
1615			if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, cmd) {
1616				continue
1617			}
1618			if len(trimmed) == len(cmd) {
1619				return true
1620			}
1621			r, _ := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(trimmed[len(cmd):])
1622			if unicode.IsSpace(r) {
1623				return true
1624			}
1625		}
1626		return false
1627	}
1628	
1629	// firstMessageAndUserCount returns the preview string and the
1630	// total number of real (non-system) user turns. The preview skips
1631	// known Claude Code command envelopes like /clear and /effort so
1632	// sessions that begin with a command still show a meaningful
1633	// preview; the user count always reflects every non-system user
1634	// turn, including skipped commands.
1635	func firstMessageAndUserCount(
1636		messages []ParsedMessage,
1637	) (string, int) {
1638		firstMsg := ""
1639		userCount := 0
1640		for _, m := range messages {
1641			if m.IsSystem {
1642				continue
1643			}
1644			if m.Role != RoleUser || m.Content == "" {
1645				continue
1646			}
1647			userCount++
1648			if firstMsg == "" &&
1649				!isSkippablePreviewCommand(m.Content) {
1650				firstMsg = truncate(
1651					strings.ReplaceAll(m.Content, "\n", " "), 300,
1652				)
1653			}
1654		}
1655		return firstMsg, userCount
1656	}
1657	
1658	// fileEndsWithNewline returns true when the byte at size-1
1659	// is '\n'. Used to distinguish a fully-flushed final line
1660	// from a truncated write. Empty files return true (no
1661	// dangling content).
1662	func fileEndsWithNewline(f *os.File, size int64) bool {
1663		if size <= 0 {
1664			return true
1665		}
1666		var b [1]byte
1667		if _, err := f.ReadAt(b[:], size-1); err != nil {
1668			return false
1669		}
1670		return b[0] == '\n'
1671	}
1672	
1673	// extractCompactSummary extracts text from a Claude compact
1674	// summary JSONL entry. Content is usually an array of content
1675	// blocks in message.content, but Claude also emits compact
1676	// summaries with content as a plain string — handle both.
1677	func extractCompactSummary(line string) string {
1678		content := gjson.Get(line, "message.content")
1679		if content.IsArray() {
1680			var parts []string
1681			content.ForEach(func(_, v gjson.Result) bool {
1682				if v.Get("type").Str == "text" {
1683					parts = append(parts, v.Get("text").Str)
1684				}
1685				return true
1686			})
1687			return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
1688		}
1689		return content.Str
1690	}
1691	
1692	// ClassifyClaudeSystemMessage inspects a user-entry content string and
1693	// returns the matched system subtype (e.g. "continuation", "resume"),
1694	// or "" if the content is an ordinary user message.
1695	//
1696	// Non-caveat <local-command-*> envelopes (stdout/stderr surrounds for
1697	// local command output) are treated as regular noise and return "";
1698	// only the caveat variant is a semantic "resume" marker.
1699	func ClassifyClaudeSystemMessage(content string) string {
1700		trimmed := strings.TrimLeftFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
1701			return r == '\uFEFF' || unicode.IsSpace(r)
1702		})
1703		switch {
1704		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "This session is being continued"):
1705			return "continuation"
1706		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<local-command-caveat>"):
1707			return "resume"
1708		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[Request interrupted"):
1709			return "interrupted"
1710		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<task-notification>"):
1711			return "task_notification"
1712		case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "Stop hook feedback:"):
1713			return "stop_hook"
1714		}
1715		return ""
1716	}
1717	
1718	// isClaudeSystemMessage returns true if the content matches
1719	// a known system-injected user message pattern.
1720	func isClaudeSystemMessage(content string) bool {
1721		trimmed := strings.TrimLeftFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
1722			return r == '\uFEFF' || unicode.IsSpace(r)
1723		})
1724		prefixes := [...]string{
1725			"This session is being continued",
1726			"[Request interrupted",
1727			"<task-notification>",
1728			"<local-command-",
1729			"Stop hook feedback:",
1730		}
1731		for _, p := range prefixes {
1732			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, p) {
1733				return true
1734			}
1735		}
1736		return false
1737	}

44		ts := parseTimestamp(gjson.Get(line, "timestamp").Str)
45		if !ts.IsZero() {
46			if b.startedAt.IsZero() {
47				b.startedAt = ts
48			}
49			b.endedAt = ts
50		}
51	
52		data := gjson.Get(line, "data")
53	
54		switch gjson.Get(line, "type").Str {
55		case copilotEventSessionStart:
56			b.handleSessionStart(data)
57		case copilotEventUserMessage:
58			b.handleUserMessage(data, ts)
59		case copilotEventAssistantMsg:
60			b.handleAssistantMessage(data, ts)
61		case copilotEventToolComplete:
62			b.handleToolComplete(data, ts)
63		case copilotEventAssistantReason:
64			b.handleAssistantReasoning()
65		case copilotEventModelChange:
66			if v := data.Get("newModel"); v.Exists() {
67				b.currentModel = v.Str
68			}
69		}
70	}

10705	fn acceptance_live_from_progress(entries: &[AcceptanceProgressEntry]) -> AcceptanceLive {

10709	        .filter_map(|entry| entry.result.clone())
10710	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

10712	        results = results.split_off(results.len() - total);
10713	    }
10714	    let passed = results.iter().filter(|result| result.passed).count();
10715	    let failed = results.iter().filter(|result| !result.passed).count();
10716	    let required_failed = results
10717	        .iter()
10718	        .filter(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
10719	        .count();
10720	    let completed = results.len();
10721	    let latest = entries.last();
10722	    let status = if required_failed > 0 {
10723	        AcceptanceUiStatus::Failed
10724	    } else if completed >= total && total > 0 {
10725	        AcceptanceUiStatus::Passed
10726	    } else if latest.is_some_and(|entry| entry.status == "running" || entry.status == "started") {
10727	        AcceptanceUiStatus::Running
10728	    } else {

10730	    };

10732	        entry
10733	            .result

10735	            .map(|result| result.detail.clone())

10741	                }
10742	            })

10749	                .result
10750	                .as_ref()

28	// build the full path for symlink resolution.
29	func isDirOrSymlink(
30		entry os.DirEntry, parentDir string,
31	) bool {
32		if entry.IsDir() {
33			return true
34		}
35		if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
36			return false
37		}
38		fi, err := os.Stat(
39			filepath.Join(parentDir, entry.Name()),

43		}

68		Root        string

73	// ResolveOpenCodeSource detects whether an OpenCode root is using
74	// file-backed storage or legacy SQLite storage.
75	func ResolveOpenCodeSource(root string) OpenCodeSource {
76		if root == "" {
77			return OpenCodeSource{}
78		}
79	
80		sessionRoot := filepath.Join(root, "storage", "session")
81		if info, err := os.Stat(sessionRoot); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
82			return OpenCodeSource{
83				Mode:        OpenCodeSourceStorage,
84				Root:        root,
85				SessionRoot: sessionRoot,
86				DBPath:      filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db"),
87			}
88		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
89			storageRoot := filepath.Join(root, "storage")
90			if info, serr := os.Stat(storageRoot); serr == nil && info.IsDir() {
91				return OpenCodeSource{
92					Mode:        OpenCodeSourceStorage,
93					Root:        root,
94					SessionRoot: sessionRoot,
95					DBPath:      filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db"),
96				}
97			}
98		}
99	
100		dbPath := filepath.Join(root, "opencode.db")
101		if info, err := os.Stat(dbPath); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
102			return OpenCodeSource{
103				Mode:   OpenCodeSourceSQLite,
104				Root:   root,
105				DBPath: dbPath,
106			}
107		}
108	
109		return OpenCodeSource{Root: root}
110	}
111	
112	// DiscoverOpenCodeSessions finds all file-backed OpenCode session
113	// JSON files under storage/session.
114	func DiscoverOpenCodeSessions(root string) []DiscoveredFile {
115		src := ResolveOpenCodeSource(root)
116		if src.Mode != OpenCodeSourceStorage {
117			return nil
118		}
119	
120		var files []DiscoveredFile
121		entries, err := os.ReadDir(src.SessionRoot)
122		if err != nil {
123			return nil
124		}
125		for _, entry := range entries {
126			if !isDirOrSymlink(entry, src.SessionRoot) {
127				continue
128			}
129			projectDir := filepath.Join(src.SessionRoot, entry.Name())
130			sessionEntries, err := os.ReadDir(projectDir)
131			if err != nil {
132				continue
133			}
134			for _, sessionEntry := range sessionEntries {
135				if sessionEntry.IsDir() ||
136					!strings.HasSuffix(sessionEntry.Name(), ".json") {
137					continue
138				}
139				path := filepath.Join(projectDir, sessionEntry.Name())
140				files = append(files, DiscoveredFile{
141					Path:    path,
142					Project: openCodeSessionProject(path),
143					Agent:   AgentOpenCode,
144				})
145			}
146		}
147	
148		sort.Slice(files, func(i, j int) bool {
149			return files[i].Path < files[j].Path
150		})

213	                .filter(|path| path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("toml"))

215	            Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(registry),

221	            }
222	        };

224	        for path in paths {

1	package parser
2	
3	// TerminationStatus describes how a parsed session appears to have
4	// ended. The empty string means "unknown" — caller should leave the
5	// stored column NULL.
6	type TerminationStatus string
7	
8	const (
9		// TerminationAwaitingUser means the agent reached a clear
10		// "I'm done, your turn" stopping point: Claude end_turn,
11		// Codex task_complete, or equivalent for other agents. UI
12		// surfaces this as a calm "waiting" indicator.
13		TerminationAwaitingUser TerminationStatus = "awaiting_user"
14	
15		// TerminationClean means the session ended for a non-orphan,
16		// non-truncated reason that ISN'T explicitly "agent waiting"
17		// (e.g. Claude max_tokens or stop_sequence). Treated as
18		// "session done" by the UI — no special indicator.
19		TerminationClean TerminationStatus = "clean"
20	
21		// TerminationToolCallPending means the last assistant message
22		// emitted a tool_use that never received a matching
23		// tool_result. Could be a tool currently running, a permission
24		// prompt waiting on the user, or a crashed agent — the JSONL
25		// can't distinguish those without runtime info.
26		TerminationToolCallPending TerminationStatus = "tool_call_pending"
27	
28		// TerminationTruncated means the session file was cut off
29		// mid-write (e.g. last line is invalid JSON).
30		TerminationTruncated TerminationStatus = "truncated"
31	)
32	
33	// Classify returns a status given a parsed message slice, the
34	// last assistant message's stop_reason (or empty when unknown),
35	// and a sentinel from the file scanner. Returns "" (unknown) when
36	// no classification can be made — for example, an empty message
37	// slice from an unparseable file. Truncation takes precedence over
38	// tool_call_pending: if the file was cut off mid-write, that's
39	// the stronger signal about what went wrong.
40	//
41	// stopReason values that signal "agent waiting on user input" map
42	// to TerminationAwaitingUser. The vocabulary differs per agent:
43	// Claude uses "end_turn"; Codex uses "task_complete"; pass through
44	// the raw string and the helper recognizes both.
45	func Classify(
46		messages []ParsedMessage,
47		stopReason string,
48		fileTruncated bool,
49	) TerminationStatus {
50		if fileTruncated {
51			return TerminationTruncated
52		}
53		if len(messages) == 0 {
54			return ""
55		}
56		if hasOrphanedToolCall(messages) {
57			return TerminationToolCallPending
58		}
59		// awaiting_user only applies when the assistant's "I'm done"
60		// signal is the actual end of the transcript. If a user
61		// message follows the last assistant turn, the agent is no
62		// longer parked — the user has already replied, so the UI
63		// should not show a "waiting for you" indicator.
64		lastIsAssistant := messages[len(messages)-1].Role == RoleAssistant
65		if lastIsAssistant && isAwaitingUserStopReason(stopReason) {
66			return TerminationAwaitingUser
67		}
68		return TerminationClean
69	}
70	
71	// isAwaitingUserStopReason reports whether the given stop_reason
72	// (from any agent's vocabulary) means the agent has finished its
73	// turn and is parked waiting for the user. The set of accepted
74	// values grows as more agents are wired up.
75	func isAwaitingUserStopReason(stopReason string) bool {
76		switch stopReason {
77		case "end_turn", // Claude
78			"task_complete": // Codex
79			return true
80		}
81		return false
82	}
83	
84	// hasOrphanedToolCall reports whether the last assistant message has
85	// any tool_use blocks that lack a matching tool_result. Only results
86	// that appear AFTER the last assistant message resolve its calls —
87	// an earlier message reusing the same ToolUseID (rare, but possible
88	// in forked sessions or malformed transcripts) must not retroactively
89	// mark the final unresolved call as resolved.
90	func hasOrphanedToolCall(messages []ParsedMessage) bool {
91		lastAssistantIdx := -1
92		for i := len(messages) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
93			if messages[i].Role == RoleAssistant {
94				lastAssistantIdx = i
95				break
96			}
97		}
98		if lastAssistantIdx == -1 {
99			return false
100		}
101		last := messages[lastAssistantIdx]
102		if len(last.ToolCalls) == 0 {
103			return false
104		}
105	
106		resolved := make(map[string]bool)
107		for _, m := range messages[lastAssistantIdx+1:] {
108			for _, tr := range m.ToolResults {
109				if tr.ToolUseID != "" {
110					resolved[tr.ToolUseID] = true
111				}
112			}
113		}
114	
115		for _, tc := range last.ToolCalls {
116			if tc.ToolUseID != "" && !resolved[tc.ToolUseID] {
117				return true
118			}
119		}
120		return false
121	}
122

12	// countingReader wraps an io.Reader and counts bytes read.
13	type countingReader struct {
14		r io.Reader
15		n int64
16	}
17	
18	func (cr *countingReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
19		n, err := cr.r.Read(p)
20		cr.n += int64(n)
21		return n, err
22	}
23	
24	// lineReader reads JSONL files line by line, skipping lines that
25	// exceed maxLen rather than aborting. The buffer starts small and
26	// grows on demand up to maxLen. After iteration, call Err() to
27	// check for I/O errors (as opposed to normal EOF).
28	type lineReader struct {
29		r         *bufio.Reader
30		cr        *countingReader
31		maxLen    int
32		buf       []byte
33		err       error
34		bytesRead int64 // total bytes consumed (from countingReader)
35	}
36	
37	func newLineReader(r io.Reader, maxLen int) *lineReader {
38		cr := &countingReader{r: r}
39		return &lineReader{
40			r:      bufio.NewReaderSize(cr, initialScanBufSize),
41			cr:     cr,
42			maxLen: maxLen,
43			buf:    make([]byte, 0, initialScanBufSize),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// next returns the next line (without trailing newline) and true,
48	// or ("", false) at EOF or read error. After the loop, call Err()
49	// to distinguish EOF from I/O failure.
50	func (lr *lineReader) next() (string, bool) {
51		for {
52			line, err := lr.readLine()
53			if err != nil {
54				if err != io.EOF {
55					lr.err = err
56				}
57				return "", false
58			}
59			if line != "" {
60				return line, true
61			}
62			// Empty line or skipped oversized line — continue.
63		}
64	}
65	
66	// Err returns the first non-EOF read error encountered, or nil.
67	func (lr *lineReader) Err() error {
68		return lr.err
69	}
70	
71	// readLine reads a full line, returning "" for blank/oversized
72	// lines and a non-nil error only at EOF or read failure.
73	// updateBytesRead computes total bytes consumed by
74	// subtracting any buffered-but-not-consumed data from the
75	// countingReader total.
76	func (lr *lineReader) updateBytesRead() {
77		if lr.cr != nil {
78			lr.bytesRead = lr.cr.n - int64(lr.r.Buffered())
79		}
80	}
81	
82	func (lr *lineReader) readLine() (string, error) {
83		lr.buf = lr.buf[:0]
84		oversized := false
85	
86		for {
87			chunk, isPrefix, err := lr.r.ReadLine()
88			if err != nil {
89				if len(lr.buf) > 0 && err == io.EOF {
90					lr.updateBytesRead()
91					break
92				}
93				return "", err
94			}
95	
96			if oversized {
97				if !isPrefix {
98					lr.updateBytesRead()
99					return "", nil // done skipping
100				}
101				continue
102			}
103	
104			lr.buf = append(lr.buf, chunk...)
105	
106			if len(lr.buf) > lr.maxLen {
107				oversized = true
108				lr.buf = lr.buf[:0]
109				if !isPrefix {
110					lr.updateBytesRead()
111					return "", nil
112				}
113				continue
114			}
115	
116			if !isPrefix {
117				lr.updateBytesRead()
118				break
119			}
120		}
121	
122		return string(lr.buf), nil
123	}
124	
125	// readJSONLFrom opens a JSONL file, seeks to offset, and
126	// calls fn for each valid JSON line. Returns the number of
127	// bytes consumed (relative to offset) and any I/O error. The
128	// returned byte count covers only complete lines, so callers
129	// can use offset+consumed as a safe resume point even if the
130	// file had a partially written line at EOF.
131	func readJSONLFrom(
132		path string, offset int64, fn func(line string),
133	) (consumed int64, err error) {
134		f, err := os.Open(path)
135		if err != nil {
136			return 0, fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", path, err)
137		}
138		defer f.Close()
139	
140		if _, err := f.Seek(offset, io.SeekStart); err != nil {
141			return 0, fmt.Errorf(
142				"seek %s to %d: %w", path, offset, err,
143			)
144		}
145	
146		lr := newLineReader(f, maxLineSize)
147		for {
148			line, ok := lr.next()
149			if !ok {
150				break
151			}
152			if gjson.Valid(line) {
153				fn(line)
154				// Track offset through last valid JSON line
155				// so partial lines at EOF are not skipped.
156				consumed = lr.bytesRead
157			}
158		}
159		return consumed, lr.Err()
160	}

20	// parseTimestamp parses a raw timestamp string into a time.Time.
21	// Returns zero time if the string is empty or unparseable.
22	func parseTimestamp(ts string) time.Time {
23		if ts == "" {
24			return time.Time{}
25		}
26		for _, layout := range timestampLayouts {
27			if t, err := time.Parse(layout, ts); err == nil {
28				return t.UTC()
29			}
30		}
31		return time.Time{}
32	}

82	pub fn restore_snapshot(state: &PipelineState, turn: u32) -> Result<()> {
83	    // REPORT.md: Infinite Undo For Agent Edits restores files from a selected
84	    // turn snapshot rather than only rewinding chat.
85	    let snapshot_dir = state
86	        .run_root
87	        .join("snapshots")
88	        .join(format!("turn-{turn}"));
89	    if !snapshot_dir.exists() {
90	        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
91	            "snapshot turn-{turn} for run {}",
92	            state.run_id
93	        )));
94	    }
95	    if state.working_dir.exists() {
96	        fs::remove_dir_all(&state.working_dir).with_path(&state.working_dir)?;
97	    }
98	    copy_tree(&snapshot_dir, &state.working_dir)
99	}
100	
101	pub fn inventory_files(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
102	    if !root.exists() {
103	        return Ok(Vec::new());
104	    }
105	    let mut files = Vec::new();
106	    for entry in WalkDir::new(root)
107	        .into_iter()
108	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
109	        .filter(|entry| entry.file_type().is_file())
110	    {
111	        files.push(entry.path().to_path_buf());
112	    }
113	    files.sort();
114	    Ok(files)
115	}
116	
117	pub fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<()> {
118	    fs::create_dir_all(to).with_path(to)?;
119	    if !from.exists() {
120	        return Ok(());
121	    }
122	    for entry in WalkDir::new(from).into_iter() {
123	        let entry = entry.map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
124	            path: from.to_path_buf(),
125	            source: source.into(),
126	        })?;
127	        let relative = entry.path().strip_prefix(from).map_err(|err| {
128	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("copy source prefix error: {err}"))
129	        })?;
130	        let target = to.join(relative);
131	        if entry.file_type().is_dir() {
132	            fs::create_dir_all(&target).with_path(&target)?;
133	        } else if entry.file_type().is_file() {
134	            if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
135	                fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
136	            }
137	            fs::copy(entry.path(), &target).with_path(&target)?;
138	        }
139	    }
140	    Ok(())
141	}

66	pub fn snapshot_working(state: &PipelineState, turn: u32) -> Result<PathBuf> {
67	    // REPORT.md: Infinite Undo For Agent Edits is implemented as durable
68	    // per-turn filesystem snapshots.

101	pub fn inventory_files(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
102	    if !root.exists() {
103	        return Ok(Vec::new());
104	    }
105	    let mut files = Vec::new();
106	    for entry in WalkDir::new(root)
107	        .into_iter()
108	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
109	        .filter(|entry| entry.file_type().is_file())
110	    {
111	        files.push(entry.path().to_path_buf());
112	    }
113	    files.sort();
114	    Ok(files)
115	}
116	
117	pub fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> Result<()> {
118	    fs::create_dir_all(to).with_path(to)?;
119	    if !from.exists() {
120	        return Ok(());
121	    }
122	    for entry in WalkDir::new(from).into_iter() {
123	        let entry = entry.map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
124	            path: from.to_path_buf(),
125	            source: source.into(),
126	        })?;
127	        let relative = entry.path().strip_prefix(from).map_err(|err| {
128	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("copy source prefix error: {err}"))
129	        })?;
130	        let target = to.join(relative);
131	        if entry.file_type().is_dir() {
132	            fs::create_dir_all(&target).with_path(&target)?;
133	        } else if entry.file_type().is_file() {
134	            if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
135	                fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
136	            }
137	            fs::copy(entry.path(), &target).with_path(&target)?;
138	        }
139	    }
140	    Ok(())
141	}

161	fn cli_provider_write_allowlist(provider: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
162	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
163	        return Vec::new();
164	    };
165	    if let Ok(registry) = ProviderRegistry::builtin()
166	        && let Some(descriptor) = registry.get(provider)
167	    {
168	        let mut paths = descriptor
169	            .sandbox_writes
170	            .iter()
171	            .map(|path| expand_home_path(path, &home))
172	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
173	        dedup_paths(&mut paths);
174	        return paths;
175	    }
176	    let mut paths = Vec::new();
177	    if provider.contains("codex") {
178	        paths.push(home.join(".codex"));
179	    }
180	    if provider.contains("claude") {
181	        paths.push(home.join(".claude"));
182	    }
183	    paths
184	}
185	
186	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path, home: &Path) -> PathBuf {
187	    if path == Path::new("~") {
188	        return home.to_path_buf();
189	    }
190	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
191	        return home.join(rest);
192	    }
193	    path.to_path_buf()
194	}
195	
196	fn push_existing_parent_roots(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>, path: &Path) {
197	    push_if_exists(paths, path);
198	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
199	        push_if_exists(paths, parent);
200	    }
201	    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) {
202	        for root in [".bun", ".local", ".npm-global", ".opencode"] {
203	            let candidate = home.join(root);
204	            if path.starts_with(&candidate) {
205	                push_if_exists(paths, candidate);
206	            }
207	        }
208	    }
209	}

## Extraction Guide: Agent CLI Discovery & Session Parsing

This guide documents the minimum facts deadreckon needs to discover session files on disk, match them to working directories, and extract per-turn activity for eight well-supported agent CLIs supported by agentsview's parser.

---

### **1. CODEX** (Canonical Reference)

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.codex/sessions/` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`. EnvVar override: `CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR`. (Registry types.go:76-89)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename stem (e.g., `session-abc123.jsonl` → session ID `abc123`, prefixed `codex:` by ParseCodexSession:1175). Fallback: `session_meta` line field `payload.id` (codex.go:122).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Codex uses `session_meta` payload's `cwd` field (early line, always populated first); also extracts git branch from `payload.git.branch` to refine project name via `ExtractProjectFromCwdWithBranch` (codex.go:124-131).

**Per-message shape:** Role (`role`: "user" or "assistant"), content (extracted from `payload.content[].text`), tool calls (`response_item.type=="function_call"` with `name` + `call_id`), tool results (`function_call_output.output`), model (`turn_context.model`), token usage (`event_msg.token_count.info.last_token_usage`), timestamp (`timestamp` ISO8601). (codex.go:88-180)

**Termination detection:** Task lifecycle events (codex.go:185): `task_started`, `task_complete`, `turn_aborted` → termination.go:74-82 maps to `awaiting_user` (task_complete), `tool_call_pending` (task_started), or unknown. Last task event signals state (classifyCodexTermination codex.go:1213-1225).

**Quirks:** Subagent spawning via `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent` calls (codex.go:218-227). Pending agent events cache notifications until matched to a wait call (codex.go:406-418). Token usage deduplication via `lastTokenUsageRaw` (codex.go:198-200). Exec-originated sessions skipped historically (now parsed; IsCodexExecSessionFile codex.go:1102-1125).

---

### **2. CLAUDE** (Claude Code)

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.claude/projects/`. EnvVar: `CLAUDE_PROJECTS_DIR`. Each project dir → multiple `*.jsonl` session files. (Registry types.go:65-75)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename stem (e.g., `abc123.jsonl` → sessionId `abc123`, no prefix for Claude). Early entries carry `sessionId` field; file derivation used when absent (claude.go:68, 197-205).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Top-level `cwd` field on first user entry (claude.go:187). Also tracks `gitBranch` for project refinement. Session metadata stored in claudeSessionMeta (claude.go:618-635).

**Per-message shape:** Role (`type`: "user" or "assistant"), content (parsed from `message.content[]` array of blocks—text, tool_use, tool_result), tool calls (content block `type=="tool_use"` with `id`, `name`, `input`), tool results (`type=="tool_result"` with `tool_use_id`), model (`message.model`), token usage (`message.usage`), stop reason (`message.stop_reason`), timestamp (`timestamp`). (claude.go:536-610, 1376-1401)

**Termination detection:** Claude.stop_reason vocabulary (Classify termination.go:45-69): `end_turn` → awaiting_user, or orphaned tool_use (hasOrphanedToolCall termination.go:90-121). File truncation detection via invalid JSON on last line without newline (claude.go:237-240).

**Quirks:** DAG-aware fork detection (uuid/parentUuid chains; claude.go:682-850). Large-gap forks (>3 user turns) split into separate sessions with `-<uuid>` suffix. Assistant message chunk merging for same-message.id within a turn (claude.go:1003-1078). Queued_command attachments (user messages typed mid-tool-call) merged by timestamp (claude.go:895-934). Compact summary boundaries marked (claude.go:510-527).

---

### **3. GEMINI**

**Storage shape:** JSON (single file per session) or JSONL. Default: `~/.gemini/tmp/`. EnvVar: `GEMINI_DIR`. Single session → one `*.json` file or JSONL stream. (Registry types.go:102-113)

**Session ID extraction:** Top-level `sessionId` field mandatory (gemini.go:77-82). No prefix.

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Project extracted from environment context; no cwd in transcripts (gemini.go:72-100). Project defaults to "gemini" when absent.

**Per-message shape:** Role (`type`: "user" or "gemini" for assistant), content (text in `content` field or content blocks array), tool calls (within `toolCalls[]` array: `id`, `name`, `args`), tool results embedded in `toolCalls[].result[].functionResponse`), model (`model` field), token usage (`tokens` object: `input`, `output`, `cached`), timestamp (`timestamp` ISO8601). (gemini.go:40-100+)

**Termination detection:** Last message's role; no explicit stop_reason vocabulary. Classify via orphaned tool calls (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Dual format support (JSON object vs. JSONL stream in same file). Thought blocks captured separately (Gemini's reasoning traces). Tool results inline in tool call definition rather than separate messages.

---

### **4. OPENCODE** (Dual Storage Modes)

**Storage shape:** Two modes detected by ResolveOpenCodeSource (discovery.go:75-110):
  - **File-based:** `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/<project>/*.json` (multiple projects, each with multiple sessions).
  - **SQLite legacy:** `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (single file, query-based).
  EnvVar: `OPENCODE_DIR`. Watch roots computed in ResolveOpenCodeWatchRoots (discovery.go:250-269).

**Session ID extraction:** File mode: filename stem `sessionid.json` (discovery.go:225-235). SQLite mode: `session.id` column query (opencode.go:42-60). Virtual path format for DB: `dbpath#sessionid` (discovery.go:271-275).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** File mode: `directory` field in JSON (opencode.go:292-300). Project from directory path or directory field via ExtractProjectFromCwd.

**Per-message shape:** File-based sessions stored as aggregated JSON. Messages extracted by query; role, content, tool data format TBD from opencode.go parser (reading first 100 lines shows sqlite/file mode dispatch but message structure deferred to later code).

**Termination detection:** SQLite: `time_updated` tracks last activity (opencode.go:88-100). File mode: relies on standard orphaned-tool logic (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Hybrid roots (storage/ + opencode.db coexist): storage canonical, SQLite fallback (discovery.go:206-239). Subdir watch path expansion (message/, part/ subdirs created lazily; discovery.go:121-126). Virtual path encoding for SQLite sessions.

---

### **5. AMP**

**Storage shape:** JSON (one thread per file). Default: `~/.local/share/amp/threads/`. EnvVar: `AMP_DIR`. Filename pattern: `T-*.json` (thread files). (Registry types.go:154-163)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename-derived ID (ampThreadIDFromPath amp.go:39). Fallback: JSON `id` field validated by isValidAmpThreadID (amp.go:42).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Project extracted from `env.initial.trees[0].displayName` (amp.go:75). No cwd in transcripts.

**Per-message shape:** Meta structure at `meta.traces[]` with traces containing `type` (Message, Action, Observation), `timestamp` (string), content in trace-specific fields. Token usage in metadata, model from trace context. Title as first message (amp.go:80+).

**Termination detection:** End time from last trace with non-empty `endTime` (amp.go:61-72). Classify via message count and last message type.

**Quirks:** Nested metadata structure (traces within meta). Thread lifecycle tracked via created (epoch ms) and endTime. Tree/project nesting in env context.

---

### **6. OPENHANDS**

**Storage shape:** Directory-per-session (UUID directory names). Default: `~/.openhands/conversations/`. EnvVar: `OPENHANDS_CONVERSATIONS_DIR`. Each session → directory with conversation files inside. (Registry types.go:131-141)

**Session ID extraction:** Directory name (validated by IsValidSessionID, discovery.go:35-36). Stored as UUID; discoverer finds directories matching UUID pattern (openhands.go:25-54).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Working directory stored in session metadata within conversation files; extraction deferred to parser.

**Per-message shape:** Message events identified by `type=="MessageEvent"` (openhands.go:18-20). Content, role (MessageEvent.role), timestamps in event entries. Tool use/result in ActionEvent/ObservationEvent (openhands.go:19-20).

**Termination detection:** Last event type determines state (MessageEvent vs. ActionEvent vs. ObservationEvent).

**Quirks:** Session as directory (not single file). Multiple file types (event log structure). Shallow watch (ShallowWatch=true Registry:138); relies on periodic sync for nested discovery.

---

### **7. IFLOW**

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.iflow/projects/`. EnvVar: `IFLOW_DIR`. Filename pattern: `session-*.jsonl`. (Registry types.go:176-185)

**Session ID extraction:** Filename: `session-<uuid>.jsonl` → trim prefix, then prepend `iflow:` (iflow.go:32-47).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Top-level `cwd` field on entries (analogous to Claude, iflow.go:55-80).

**Per-message shape:** Similar to Claude: `type` (user/assistant), `message.content[]` blocks (text, tool_use, tool_result), uuid/parentUuid DAG structure, timestamps. Tool calls in content blocks (iflow.go:18-25).

**Termination detection:** uuid/parentUuid chain forms streaming snapshots, not forks—no fork splitting applied (iflow.go:27-31). Termination via lastTaskEvent or orphaned tools.

**Quirks:** DAG structure is sliding-window snapshot stream, not conversation forks—parse linearly without fork detection. Similar message structure to Claude but different semantic interpretation of uuid chains.

---

### **8. COPILOT**

**Storage shape:** JSONL format (append-only). Default: `~/.copilot/session-state/`. EnvVar: `COPILOT_DIR`. WatchSubdirs: `["session-state"]`. (Registry types.go:91-101)

**Session ID extraction:** JSONL `type==session.start` event carries `data.sessionId` (copilot.go:54-70, 75-76).

**cwd/working-dir matching:** Session start event's `data.context.cwd` + `context.branch` (copilot.go:79-80).

**Per-message shape:** Event-based: `type` determines message type (user.message, assistant.message, tool.execution_complete, assistant.reasoning, session.model_change). Role implicit in event type. Content in `data` object. Tool calls/results in tool.execution_complete events (copilot.go:13-21, 42-70).

**Termination detection:** Model from session.model_change; last event type signals state. Orphaned tools via standard logic (termination.go:90-121).

**Quirks:** Event-stream format (not message-centric). Session lifecycle marked by session.start event. Tool execution as discrete events, not message-embedded blocks.

---

### **Shared Infrastructure**

**linereader.go** (Line-by-line JSONL parsing): newLineReader manages buffered scanning with a configurable max line size (64MB) and graceful oversized-line skipping. readJSONLFrom enables offset-based resume for incremental parsing (linereader.go:37-160). Used by all JSONL parsers (Codex, Claude, iFlow, Copilot).

**timestamp.go** (Uniform timestamp parsing): parseTimestamp tries eight ISO8601 variants in priority order (RFC3339Nano, RFC3339, milliseconds, zone variants, space-separated) to accommodate agent diversity (timestamp.go:10-32). Used across all agents; logParseError flags unparseable strings.

**termination.go** (Unified termination classification): Classify function (termination.go:45-69) maps message sequence + stop_reason + file truncation → TerminationStatus enum (awaiting_user, clean, tool_call_pending, truncated). isAwaitingUserStopReason (termination.go:75-82) unifies agent vocabularies (Claude "end_turn", Codex "task_complete"). hasOrphanedToolCall (termination.go:90-121) detects unresolved tool_use blocks after last assistant message.

**discovery.go** (Session file discovery & location): DiscoverFunc/FindSourceFunc pairs (Registry AgentDef types.go:52-59) handle agent-specific filesystem layout. UUID regex uuidRe (discovery.go:20-24) matches session identifiers. ResolveOpenCodeSource (discovery.go:75-110) dual-mode detection. Helper isDirOrSymlink (discovery.go:29-45) normalizes directory checks. ExtractProjectFromCwd/NormalizeName infer project names from filesystem paths.

**taxonomy.go** (Tool normalization): NormalizeToolCategory (taxonomy.go:8-206) is the **single source of truth** for raw tool name → canonical category mapping across all agents (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Task, Tool, Other). Agents emit names like "shell_command" (Codex), "run_command" (Gemini), "bash" (OpenCode), "Shell" (Cursor) → all map to "Bash". Subagent detection via substring match (line 201) captures MCP-prefixed tools and spawn_subagent naming patterns.

---

**Summary:** Deadreckon can implement per-agent discovery and parsing by adopting agentsview's Registry pattern (agent type → storage dirs → discovery func → parse func), reusing timestamp and termination logic, and mapping raw tool names through NormalizeToolCategory. The dual-mode OpenCode strategy (file vs. SQLite) and Claude's DAG fork splitting represent the most complex behaviors; other agents follow more linear parsing paths. Each agent's session_meta carries cwd; combined with git branch metadata, this enables robust working-directory attribution.
